context.text: iCloud isn't for keeping photos permanently. Bring into iPhoto [Mac] or Photo Gallery [part of MS Essentials, Windows] for permanent storage. After transfer choice to delete copies on phone.
Tap Share button, select photos you want to delete by tapping on them and then tap Delete.

iCloud is a syncing system not a just backup. If you delete pictures on your iPhone (assuming logged into same iCloud account) you're also deleting pictures in iCloud. This not what you want to do. Find backup solution to keep photos like Dropbox or Amazon Photos. Those allow you upload images without keeping them on other devices.

Deleting photos on phone WILL delete iCloud copy. Instead open Settings > iCloud > photos check option "optimize iPhone storage". This supposed to allow phone to have smaller photo files, while original resolution maintained in iCloud copy.

You didn't say what version of iOS or macOS you're using nor did mention if used iCloud or not. This answer applies to latest versions of all. If currently using iCloud to sync photos across devices, once you delete a photo on any those devices, it will also delete on iCloud. Here Apple site about iCloud and how to use it. iCloud is a syncing system to give access to all content regardless of device using. If want to delete photo from device but keep it in cloud solution, need to use a 3rd-party cloud service. Services as Dropbox or Onebox can be used as backup/storage solution.

To strictly answer your question, not possible to delete something from your device have it remain accessible from iCloud Photo Library. more details: idea behind iCloud Photos Library is to have all your photos on all your devices. Picture a parent of a small family in California who takes, on average, several photos a week has a Mac, iPad, and iPhone. When they take a photo on their iPhone, it syncs to their other two devices automatically so when they arrive home, they can open computer and view photos or videos they took. cool? Yes, for some situations it's ideal. But problem, if you don't have enough storage on phone to hold all photos, iCloud Library stuck until you open settings and allow it to optimize your device storage. It then saves low resolution photos to device download high resolution version when you view photo. convenient in some situations. problem comes in when you want to control what photos go where. I've taken thousands of photos and videos on my iPhone don't want all of those on my phone. But with iCloud Library enabled, all of photos will be on your device no way to control what images are in cloud versus on your device., seems Apple's solution to problem of having too many photos and videos on phone would be to enable option to optimize device storage. However, by, biggest problem with iCloud Photo Library and "optimize device storage" option. If you enable that setting, and then to disable it at, it will attempt to download full resolution version of all your images (not just device-optimized high-resolution one). This, but causes problem as your device likely wouldn't have near enough storage by to handle that., probably not the approach you want to take. To summarize: use iCloud Photo Library if you don't take (or keep) a lot of photos and if have more than one Apple device. Otherwise, better to avoid it.

you sync your photos to iCloud, it be automatically get stored in iCloud drive. Once you stop syncing phone with iCloud drive, photos you already synced will be there, not be deleted with user permission.
For laptop, move photos to separate folder, desktop for easily finding it, then delete them from iCloud. On your phone, just upload photos to laptop delete them from phone, turn off photos in iCloud.

On your phone, open Photos app select Albums from bottom. One of albums is Recently Deleted. Once you delete photos from there, sync phone, they should all be off phone. Recently Deleted album appears to work like a trash can for deleted photos and videos, but with 30 day expiration. If photo or video isn't recovered from Recently Deleted within 30 days, then it is removed from phone.

Enter and Return often interchangeable, particularly on Windows systems distinction less obvious with some other OS. key is in codes keys send when you press them - we all know what we intend, when we use those keys, but what does computer see? answer is is either sees a command for New Line, or a Carriage Return. These 2 separate commands do different things - think of a typewriter; new line is like advancing barrel moving paper up one line, carriage return returns whole sheet of paper back to left margin as as advancing paper up. symbols almost reflect this; ↩ (new line and return) or (doesn't indicate new line, but indicate stationary cursor; see example later) Now, sometimes (Yep, Windows) no matter what you input, you get a carriage return, as OS doesn't distinguish between the 2. But on other OS it give 2 different meanings., an Enter often used to move onto next item, with Return signifying an end to input and return to beginning. difference between the 2 in many programs might be something like the following: Dear Sirs,  What's difference between Enter and Return? Many Thanks,  Stuffe Or Dear Sirs, ↩ What's difference between Enter and Return?↩ Thanks, ↩ Stuffe↩ isn't quite clean analogy on modern systems, but that's historical starter for 10. get's muddled by fact, these days we often use TAB in place of Enter, think of filling a web form in.

I see it, forwarding applies to forwarding at any layer. A frame/packet/cell arrives at a device, a header address is inspected address is looked up in forwarding table, forwarding decision is made and datagram is sent out of interface on its way. Routing describes this function when forwarding decision is made at layer 3, using IP destination address. Switching and bridging refer to forwarding decision made at layer 2, using destination MAC address. some confusion around this as seen layer 3 forwarding referred to as switching when carried out on an L3 switch.
Routing - Packets forwarded by layer 3 gateway, router. Switching - Frames forwarded by layer 2 switch. Forwarding - Protocol Data Units forwarded by networked / networking device.

If limited to these two definitions, first is closest. But, historically, application of "terminal" to computer systems derived from more general use in field of telecommunications. In context, as Wikipedia defines it, In context of telecommunications, a terminal is device which ends a telecommunications link is point at signal enters and/or leaves network. Examples of equipment containing network terminations are telephones, fax machines, computer terminals network devices, printers and workstations. first computer terminals were teleprinters (Teletypes) origins with Samuel Morse and telegraph networks of 19th century. Terminal programs in modern operating systems connect to channel called a PTY, or psuedo-teletype. terminal programs emulate physical terminals (teletypes followed by graphical displays) once connected to mainframe.

, forwarding refers to a device sending a datagram to next device in path to destination, switching refers to moving a datagram from one interface to another within device, routing refers to process a layer-3 device uses to decide on what to with a layer-3 packet. A host sending data to another host through ethernet interface will place a frame on wire. If next device is a bridge (a switch is a bridge), bridge will inspect the frame for source and destination MAC addresses. bridge use source MAC address in its MAC address table so it knows host with that MAC address is connected to interface where frame entered bridge. It will also try to look up destination MAC address in MAC address table to see to which interface it should switch the frame. If it finds MAC address in MAC address table, it will switch frame to interface indicated in MAC address table, otherwise it will flood frame to all other interfaces, forwarding frame to device(s) on other end(s) of interface(s) link(s). A router receiving a frame on interface will strip frame from packet. router try to look up destination IP address in routing table. If it doesn't find a match, even default route, it will drop the packet. If it finds one or more matches, it will switch packet to interface of the longest match in routing table. router prepare a new frame for packet on new interface (the link on new interface may or may not use MAC addresses), router will forward the new frame containing original packet over next hop interface toward destination. The whole process router uses is called routing, but within router, it switches packets before forwarding them to next hop device.

If you point static route to broadcast interface, route inserted into routing table only when broadcast interface is up. This configuration not recommended because when next hop of static route points to interface, router considers each hosts within range of route to be directly connected through interface. For example, ip route 0. 0. 0. 0 0. 0. 0. 0 Ethernet0. With this type configuration, router performs Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) on Ethernet for every destination router finds through default route because router considers all destinations as directly connected to Ethernet 0. This default route, especially if used by lot of packets to many different destination subnets, can cause high processor utilization large ARP cache (along with attendant memory allocation failures). Specifying numerical next hop on directly connected interface prevents router from performing ARP or each destination address. However, if interface with next hop goes down and numerical next hop is reachable through recursive route, should specify both next hop IP address and interface through which next hop should be found. For example, ip route 0. 0. 0. 0 0. 0. 0. 0 Serial 3/3 192. 168. 20. 1. Excerpt from Specifying a Next Hop IP Address for Static Routes at cisco. com

Saved forms and cookies not same thing. Cookies (for example) keep you logged in to website, instead of re-log-in every time visit. Saved forms are Safari's way keeping text in login form, so when you logged out don't need to enter credentials again. It sounds like you're talking about saved forms. To make sure this working, go to Safari > Preferences > AutoFill "User names and passwords" is checked.

Depending on browser using, password may stored in data structures. Apple Safari - Go Preferences > Passwords tab Google Chrome - Go Preferences > Settings > Show Advanced Settings. link > Passwords and forms > Manage Passwords link Mozilla Firefox - Preferences > Security tab > Saved Passwords button
It saves site for which you don't want to save password, not password itself. can see sites at: Safari->Preferences->Passwords

Usually, password isn't stored in cookie. You login to example. com with your username and password, these verified to belong to you (typically by hashing your password and checking hash of password matches with hash for a user with username), server issues you a long random number token as a secret identifier for you. they choose 24 random characters from 62 characters (26 uppercase letters, 26 lowercase letters, 10 numbers). They store this identifier in their database as valid and associated with you. Every time you make a request while logged in - you send cookie to your website. Every time request sent in with this identifier, they look up if its associated with valid logged-in user, if it is they give information about user. There are 6224 ~ 1043 ~ 2142 possibilities. If your website has a billion (10^9) signed in users at who were issued tokens, you'd have to try roughly 10^37 possibilities until'd lucky enough to randomly guess one. (If each try takes 1 nanosecond, take about 1011 billion years before you lucky to guess a valid token). session cookie typically only valid for a certain amount of time, also stored in server side database. other variations on this theme, e. g., using HMAC (hash message authentication codes) with stored timestamp based on server-side secret. when you login server gives you timestamp strong hash of timestamp and your username combined with server side secret. server calculates h=HMAC(secret + timestamp + username) when you login, gives you back calculated h -- then you send (h, username, and timestamp) as your login information. (And server takes your username and timestamp, recalculates h compares it to h you gave, makes sure timestamp is still valid and not very old). not familiar with particulars of how stackexchange does it (e. g., what the t=.. &s=. part of. security. stackexchange. com), but its probably a variation on this scheme. it does not encrypt your username or password in recoverable way -- it either stored in a database or based on one-way hash function relies on server-side secret.
Session cookies only stored in memory, rest in ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Cookies, it's an sqlite3 database.

This is, technically, not an answer but might be a reason why some sites do not save passwords. They (those web sites/pages) have code to tell browser to not save password. Possibly a password manager might do that for you (there free ones, I believe) or google-fu might find that bit JavaScript that worked time in telling sites to stop telling browser to not save password.

In some cases website itself telling browser to not save passwords. number of ways a web programmer can implement this and number of ways to get around it. I used to use little JavaScript "bookmarklet" tried to turn off any JavaScript on website that told browser to not save password. worked about a quarter of the time. Barely worth trouble. More recently moved to 3rd party password manager (1Password) that will save password for any website. Editing preference file is chancy and annoyingly "manual" but possible (EG worth looking into if it possible) depending on how geeky you want to get. checking for preferences say not to remember password for specific site in Keychain or Safari is worth checking on. But my bet is on a website telling browser not to remember passwords.

Safari stores passwords in OSX Keychain. Open /Applications/Utilities/Keychain Access. app, select "Login" keychain (this should be default) select "Passwords" under "Category". Doubleclick entry check "Show password"; you'll be asked for login keychain password (this usually same as account password). (For while I was using add-on for Firefox used Keychain, but it was highly broken. )
passwords still saved in Keychain, not a separate 'new' location. Safari 6 includes new front end for accessing them directly without having to go to Keychain Access application.

setting is in Safari, not Keychain. Open Safari > Preferences. > Passwords. You will see list of sites is searchable. Usually, password isn't stored in cookie. You login to example. com with your username and password, these verified to belong to you (typically by hashing your password and checking hash of password matches with hash for a user with username), server issues you a long random number token as a secret identifier for you. they choose 24 random characters from 62 characters (26 uppercase letters, 26 lowercase letters, 10 numbers). They store this identifier in their database as valid and associated with you. Every time you make a request while logged in - you send cookie to your website. Every time request sent in with this identifier, they look up if its associated with valid logged-in user, if it is they give information about user. There are 6224 ~ 1043 ~ 2142 possibilities. If your website has a billion (10^9) signed in users at who were issued tokens, you'd have to try roughly 10^37 possibilities until'd lucky enough to randomly guess one. (If each try takes 1 nanosecond, take about 1011 billion years before you lucky to guess a valid token). session cookie typically only valid for a certain amount of time, also stored in server side database. other variations on this theme, e. g., using HMAC (hash message authentication codes) with stored timestamp based on server-side secret. when you login server gives you timestamp strong hash of timestamp and your username combined with server side secret. server calculates h=HMAC(secret + timestamp + username) when you login, gives you back calculated h -- then you send (h, username, and timestamp) as your login information. (And server takes your username and timestamp, recalculates h compares it to h you gave, makes sure timestamp is still valid and not very old). not familiar with particulars of how stackexchange does it (e. g., what the t=.. &s=. part of. security. stackexchange. com), but its probably a variation on this scheme. it does not encrypt your username or password in recoverable way -- it either stored in a database or based on one-way hash function relies on server-side secret.

CSRF protection not used to protect data. used to protect user from unknowingly changing state, transferring money or logging out of account., if your GET request changing state (which shouldn't be), you should have CSRF protection. if just returning data, doesn't need CSRF protection, because CSRF protection wouldn't protect anything in this case. may help to go over this page again: https://www. owasp. org/index. php/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_%28CSRF%29

CSRF protection only needed for state-changing operations because of same-origin policy. This policy states: a web browser permits scripts in a first web page to access data in second web page, but only if both web pages have same origin. CSRF attack not to access data it requests because it is a cross-site (that CS in CSRF) request and prohibited by same-origin policy. illicit data access not a problem with CSRF. CSRF attack can execute commands but can't see results, it forced to act blindly. For example, CSRF attack can tell your browser to request bank account balance, but it can't see that balance. This is a pointless attack (unless're trying to DDoS bank server or). But not pointless if, for example, CSRF attack tells your browser to instruct your bank to transfer money from your account to attacker's account. success or failure page for transfer is inaccessible to attacking script. for attacker, they don't need to see bank's response, they just want money in their account. only state-changing operations are likely to be targets of CSRF attacks, only they need CSRF defenses.

safe methods do not to be protected against CSRF they do not make changes to application, even if returning sensitive information protected by Same Origin Policy in browser. If your site implemented as per standards, your GET requests should be safe do not need protection. However, specific case where "Cross-Site DoS"* attack could be executed. Say your reporting page takes 10 seconds to execute, with 100% CPU usage on database server, and 80% CPU usage on web server. Users your website know never to go to https://yoursite. example. org/Analysis/GetReport during office hours because it kills server gives bad user experience., Chuck wants to knock your yoursite. example. org website offline he doesn't like you or your company. On busy forum he posts to often, http://forum. walkertexasranger. example. com, he sets his signature to following: He know your company employees frequent forum, often while logged into yoursite. example. org. Every time of Chuck's posts are read by employees, authentication cookies are sent to https://yoursite. example. org/Analysis/GetReport, your site processes request and generates report, your system goes offline because CPU is eaten by these constant requests. even though request is a GET request doesn't make permanent changes to system (aka "safe"), it is infact bringing down your system every time ran., better to protect this with CSRF prevention method. *XSDoS, or Cross-Site Denial if Service, is a phrase coined by me, don't go Googling for it.

CSRF, or Cross-Site Request Forgery, isn't about protecting data from retrieved, but protecting data from being changed. also referred to as state changes. In application, state changes can include profile data, like email address, user password, biography, transferring funds. GET requests used for idempotent requests, or requests do not change state. requests do not need to have anti-CSRF tokens. POST requests used for non-idempotent requests, or requests do change state.

From man grep: egrep is same as grep -E. fgrep same as grep -F. Direct invocation as either egrep or fgrep deprecated, but provided to allow historical applications rely on them to run unmodified. use fgrep or grep -F if don't want grepped string to interpreted as a pattern. use egrep or grep -E if need to use extended regexp.

From "man grep": three variant programs egrep, fgrep rgrep available. egrep same as grep -E. fgrep same as grep -F. rgrep same as grep -r. Direct invocation as either egrep or fgrep deprecated, but provided to allow historical applications rely on them to run unmodified.

egrep fgrep equivalent to grep -E grep -F (respectively): -E, --extended-regexp Interpret PATTERN as extended regular expression (ERE, see below). (-E specified by POSIX. ) -F, --fixed-strings Interpret PATTERN as list of fixed strings, separated by newlines, any to be matched. (-F specified by POSIX. ) Error messages might differ.

egrep is 100% equivalent to grep -E fgrep is 100% equivalent to grep -F Historically these switches provided in separate binaries. On some old Unix systems need to call separate binaries, but on all modern systems switches preferred. man page for grep has details about this. for, -E switches grep into a special mode so expression evaluated as an ERE (Extended Regular Expression) as opposed to normal pattern matching. Details of syntax on man page. -E, --extended-regexp Interpret PATTERN as an extended regular expression -F switch switches grep into a different mode it accepts a pattern to match, but splits pattern up into one search string per line and does OR search on any strings without special pattern matching. -F, --fixed-strings Interpret PATTERN as a list of fixed strings, separated by newlines, any of which is to be matched. example scenarios: You have a file with list of say ten Unix usernames in plain text. want to search group file on machine to see if any of ten users listed are in any special groups: grep -F -f user_list. txt /etc/group -F switch helps is usernames in pattern file interpreted as plain text strings. Dots for example interpreted as dots rather than wild-cards. want to search using fancy expression. For example parenthesis () can be used to indicate groups with | used as an OR operator. could run this search using -E: grep -E '^no(fork|group)' /etc/group. to return lines that start with either "nofork" or "nogroup". Without -E switch to escape special characters involved because with normal pattern matching they would just search for exact pattern; grep '^no\(fork\|group\)' /etc/group

In nutshell, grep does one thing only as many other UNIX tools that's matching a line to given pattern it does it well. other, awk is more sophisticated tool it is a complete programming language defined by POSIX standard with typical features like variables, arrays, expressions, functions control statements for pattern scanning and processing. In, it depends on implementation how both tools perform in case of pattern matching on size of input to process. expect grep is usually more efficient than awk it does matching only. But can't write with grep simple code to perform more complex tasks like further processing of matched records, computation or printing results without using other tools.

If you search for verbatim string, want to be sure string you passed is interpreted verbatim (i. e. without risking say dot or question mark be interpreted as something else) use fgrep or egrep -F. for difference between egrep and grep, I think egrep is most of the time the thing you want. GNU manual site lists differences between grep and egrep seems to lay in syntax: some things require slashes other do not. egrep is more "compatible" with perl regexps and javascript regexps easier to me to use egrep. Btw. encourage you to give ack a try - it supports PREGs, has more useful defaults (i. e. coloring, skipping probably-not-what-you-want directories like. svn, ability to follow symlinks, easier to type ack than grep -E).

shell expands subexpression $file on right hand side of pipe before variable has any value. in both functions egrep is called with empty string in place of $file. first function doesn't throw error because empty pattern is valid parameter for egrep both on macOS and on Linux. In second fucntion difference comes into play because empty subexpression causes BSD egrep (the one used on macOS) to throw error. Example: echo foo | egrep "|foo" egrep: empty (sub)expression as another example with $file no value echo foo | egrep "$file|foo" egrep: empty (sub)expression, as workaround in function use: egrep -e "$file" -e 'OK' no idea why you using egrep when looking for fixed strings.

Long Answer SDD (Spinning Disc Drive) - a. k. a HDD (Hard Disc Drive) important to know difference between Spinning Disc Drive (SDD) and Solid State Drive (SSD) answer What is a Spinning Disc Drive? Spinning Disc Drives have moving parts Spinning Disc Drives phased out in favor of Solid State Drives (at in consumer applications) SSD (Solid State Drive) SSD means "a hard drive without moving parts" Solid State Drive developed to improve upon Spinning Disc Drives (moving parts not reliable and slow to read from memory) SSD has been around for decades (contrary to popular belief) Recently, technology gotten better, see them in all newer comptuers RAM (Random Access Memory) SSD's originally achieved by using RAM as method to store data RAM requires continuous power to applied to retain data By using RAM, hard drive no longer had moving parts major downside of using RAM: can never turn hard drive off or else lose all data. Historically, RAM was/is used in conjunction with Spinning Disc Drive or Solid State Drive (since RAM cannot retain data once powered off) upside of using RAM: RAM is super fast - faster than SSD's and flash memory Flash Storage Flash storage is old technology, started as way to permanently store information without power continuously applied (in contrast to RAM) Flash storage traditionally had significant aging issues could only write to memory certain number of times before lose section of drive, and performance worse over time.Flash storage improved (in late 2000’s), manufacturers started making SSDs out of Flash memory instead of out of RAM. This means worse performance for USB's than SSD's (but believe current USB technology is improving to close gap) SUMMARY SSD means a hard disk doesn’t have moving parts; Flash is type of memory fast and doesn’t require continuous power (non-volatile) SSDs used to use RAM, but now use Flash instead. In, shouldn’t compare Flash to SSD just as shouldn’t compare batteries to lithium-ion. In both cases latter is a type of the former.

Features are what your program can do. Features direct result of user requirements, and business objectives. a program's features exist mainly to meet user demands. Functionality, on other hand, is how features are implemented.
Features are what sales people sell. Functions programmers develop.

Functions don't fit into context user story are mostly transparent to user. Tasks are individual units of work must be completed to deliver either a feature or function. In my projects I not to differentiate between a Feature and a Function I write user stories for features add functions or refactoring efforts as Tasks to complete a single feature. This sometimes makes certain features look bloated on project plan but this is okay, because if I need Functions 1 and 2 and Function 3 to be refactored to deliver Feature 1 perhaps my only deliverable for sprint will be Feature 1, or possibly no deliverables at all. A function is takes inputs returns one or more values. If returned values entirely determined by inputs, function doesn't have side effects (logging, perhaps, or causing state changes outside itself), then it's called a pure function. A procedure is a function that doesn't return a value., this means procedure can only cause side effects. (That might include mutating input parameter!) A method is function that closes over a set of variables, a closure. It takes zero or more input parameters, has access to set variables, returns zero or more values. In OO languages methods are attached to objects or classes. In most mainstream OO languages, closed-over variables are called member fields, or instance variables, of an object. A method can be a pure function, impure function or a procedure. latter definition leads to object = struct + closures correspondence.

A function is takes inputs returns one or more values. If returned values entirely determined by inputs, function doesn't have side effects (logging, perhaps, or causing state changes outside itself), then it's called a pure function. A procedure is a function that doesn't return a value., this means procedure can only cause side effects. (That might include mutating input parameter!) A method is function that closes over a set of variables, a closure. It takes zero or more input parameters, has access to set variables, returns zero or more values. In OO languages methods are attached to objects or classes. In most mainstream OO languages, closed-over variables are called member fields, or instance variables, of an object. A method can be a pure function, impure function or a procedure. latter definition leads to object = struct + closures correspondence.

no portable ps program. ps command available on linux is, as others mentioned, from "procps" package. reason this cannot be ported to OSX is because Linux and OSX kernels do not expose this information in same way. Linux uses pseudo-filesystem in /proc, whereas OSX uses sysctl function. Other systems may use either mechanism but provide data in different format, or may require programs like ps to read directly from kernel's memory. In no standard for how process information available to programs like ps and top; program has to be designed for specific operating system. If specific feature missing from OSX ps, you'll have to find another program can do it, or write one yourself (look at sysctl manual, in particular KERN_PROC as starting point), or modify existing ps command to add feature. Alternately, if you can get what need by parsing output of ps command itself, you may be to write a portable program - output with -o option is reasonably reliable across platforms, particularly if refer to UNIX standard for column names to use.

A protocol is not a set of rules. protocol is thing those rules describe rules of. This why programs implement protocol comply with standard. Protocols like languages. Standards like dictionaries. For example, by analogy: This answer = A web page English language = HTTP protocol Rules of English = HTTP standard
protocol defines set of rules used by two or more parties to interact between themselves. A standard is formalized protocol accepted by most parties implement it.

In my understanding, a protocol describes communication between two points. One point creates data other point must interpret. protocol describes data format, states, requests and answers, on. E. g. a HTTP request from client and answer from server. For a specific problem, there are a gazillion possible protocols. Out, a standard chooses one specific protocol makes it mandatory. If all communication end points act accordingly to standard, they can communicate with each other and understand each other. This can happen officially or unofficially, because all communication partners happen to use same protocol which then became standard protocol.
Not all protocols are standards (some proprietary). Not standards (some govern other layers than communcation).

Communication protocols are, by definition, sets of rules govern formats and interactions between communicating parties. These rules may be implicit and informal, as in typical everyday social interactions between people. But electronics, digital computers especially, require more explicit and formalized for reliable communication. A Standard is an attempt to resolve potential misunderstanding or disagreement. Communication protocols are one of many areas that standards may apply to. notable standards are not communication protocols, for, are the SI weight and measurement standards. These provide a fixed reference to can compare any given quantity to measure it in a way unambiguous to everyone with access to standard, or reasonable approximation. A Communication Protocol Standard is a formalization of rules of a communication protocol those with access to standard can unambiguously determine whether any attempt at communication complies with those rules. Just as comparing a particular mass of metal against SI standard kilogram will determine how close mass is to kilogram, comparing a particular protocol implementation against a protocol standard will determine whether it is truly following that protocol according to standard. When all parties are properly following the protocol as formalized in standard, it is, ideally guaranteed to result in level of communication that the protocol was designed to accommodate. A Communication Protocol Specification is a means by rules and formats of a communication protocol can be described at a formal level, it is often part of, largest part of a communication protocol standard. purpose of a standard is to create a means to determine whether something is truly an instance of the standardized thing, purpose of specification is to define exactly what the thing is in case where thing is defined by rules formats, as communication protocol is. An unambiguous definition of what something is can be used to create a new instance of thing and to determine whether an existing thing is an instance of thing being defined.a specification can be used as a standard, but being a standard also carries weight of social agreement value in complying with specification well enough for multiple implementations to assurance of working together. parties interested in this agreement work together to form a Standards Body in to define standards they will agree on for purpose of their desire to be to rely on compliance to a protocol. Without presence of this social agreement and standards body by standards are produced, protocol specifications aren't generally considered to constitute standards, though well-defined specifications have potential to be used as standards.

In practice, TCP easier to police in a firewalled network: Traffic pertaining to externally vs internally established connections, client vs server roles, can be clearly distinguished handled by separate policy. For example, can ensure hosts on protected network can access external web server but not to act as web server to outside clients. For UDP services (for example DNS), enforcing such policies requires more intelligence and guesswork, since to take information above and below transport layer into account.

protocol number used by layer-3 protocol (IPv4 or IPv6) to determine to which layer-4 protocol in network stack it should send payload of packet. port number is an address for some layer-4 protocols (TCP or UDP). port number used by layer-4 protocol to determine which application gets payload of layer-4 datagram. routing protocol use protocol number in TCP header. believe you confusing layer-3 and layer-4. TCP header (layer 4) doesn't have field for protocol number - protocol number is in IP header (layer 3). Layers 2 to 4 each encapsulate datagram of layer above inside headers for layer. See this question and answer for more detail

remember models like OSI are just, models. theoretical. real world doesn't fall neatly into these models. For most part, routing is a layer-3 function, but, pointed out, BGP uses layer-4 protocol to communicate with other BGP speakers to do normally considered a layer-3 function. Many network protocols fall into gray area, or are considered in one layer while using another layer. Take ARP for instance. It resolves layer-3 addresses to layer-2 addresses. Which layer should it be considered to in? Understanding models is useful, but models are not mandated by organization, you free to create protocols and functions that do not follow any model.

Is TCP more secure than UDP? Yes, but we to be clear about what we are talking about talking about "security" not generalize this statement to upper layer protocols. Currently, security is often associated to CIA triad: Confidentiality. Integrity. Availability. version 4 of IP protocol, still most commonly used now, is a very old beast developed during 70's and 80's. At that time, confidentiality was not really a subject targeted was to achieve integrity and availability (the Arpanet network, ancestor of Internet gave birth to IP protocol, designed to ensure continuity of service even in of nuclear war, not to protect in-transit data). In this optic, two transport protocols developed over IP layer: TCP and UDP. TCP was one designed to ensure both integrity and availability properties. It includes at advanced techniques as three-way handshake, parameters negotiation, various connection state handling, transparent packet reordering, acknowledgement windows and retry mechanisms. This brings good guaranties to sender that data it sent has received in complete an uncorrupted form (ie. no missing, altered or unordered parts). Remind this protocol was targeting was technical disaster, not malicious tampering of data in transit. Such issue out-of-scope at that time. UDP on contrary was designed to be a fast protocol. It has none of above mentioned feature, and therefore none of their overhead too. In, when sender sends some data using UDP, data received may be incomplete, unordered or not received at all: UDP protocol by does not provide any mechanism to prevent or detect this neither on sender or receiver sides. In, when focusing on data integrity and availability properties of security, TCP is indeed more secure than UDP. Is application protocol relying on TCP more secure than one relying on UDP? Certainly not.means people developing application protocol relying on UDP will have more work since they may to implement in application protocol workarounds for features missing in UDP protocol. They to take into account data sent may not be necessarily received, data received may not be in right order, etc. These all well-known problems. OpenVPN for, supports TCP mostly for compatibility with restrictive firewalls, runs by default runs best over UDP. Switching it to TCP is possible but not increase its security as difference between two transport layer protocol UDP and TCP is fully handled by OpenVPN. Switching it to TCP will only add TCP overhead to OpenVPN protocol, reducing its performance. Is TCP better than UDP? No, this is entirely an application protocol design choice. UDP is a more raw protocol. When used correctly and carefully it may achieve better performances than TCP at price of more difficult development and maintenance of application protocol. When application is not time sensitive, TCP imposes itself as natural choice no need to reinvent the wheel. When application is time sensitive, discussion must occur on which to choose knowing each will with drawback: potential performance penalty with TCP against more complex application with UDP. Most protocols are not time sensitive TCP is most widely used protocol., when you load a web page or receive email, no difference if you receive it 10 milliseconds sooner or later. Two classical examples of protocols using UDP, in to OpenVPN cited, are media streaming and DNS. With media streaming, you don't care if one video frame or few milliseconds of video or audio is missing, as long as video or audio is playing smoothly and synchronously. In case, you don't want to induce repetitive pauses because TCP detected missing packet and asked sender to resend content of last acknowledgement window.With DNS, requests and answers usually short you want name resolution process to fast as possible (note longer and less time-sensitive answers such as DNS zone transfers usually still occur on TCP). faster to resend name resolution request to DNS server on very few times request or answer gets lost than processing full-fledged three-way handshake for every request. What about confidentiality and malicious sniffing/tampering (and IPv6)? All cared about until now was, in spirit of old IPv4, balance between transmission speed and data integrity + availability. Now, if want to add confidentiality on top of this, we can do this but it will have to be done at application layer as, as stated before, IPv4 not concerned by confidentiality issues. modern, full-fledged implementation of security can be implemented at application layer rely on either TCP or UDP (or both) protocols without impact on application protocol security (see example of OpenVPN above). However, as stated in beginning, IPv4 comes from another computing age. got successor by name if IPv6, natively supports IPSec at IP layer, providing more modern security services below transport protocols such as UDP and TCP. This allows to delegate in-transit data encryption from application to network layer, allows both UDP and TCP to provide same security guaranties. protocol defines set of rules used by two or more parties to interact between themselves. A standard is formalized protocol accepted by most parties implement it.

In my understanding, a protocol describes communication between two points. One point creates data other point must interpret. protocol describes data format, states, requests and answers, on. E. g. a HTTP request from client and answer from server. For a specific problem, there are a gazillion possible protocols. Out, a standard chooses one specific protocol makes it mandatory. If all communication end points act accordingly to standard, they can communicate with each other and understand each other. This can happen officially or unofficially, because all communication partners happen to use same protocol which then became standard protocol.
Not all protocols are standards (some proprietary). Not standards (some govern other layers than communcation).

Communication protocols are, by definition, sets of rules govern formats and interactions between communicating parties. These rules may be implicit and informal, as in typical everyday social interactions between people. But electronics, digital computers especially, require more explicit and formalized for reliable communication. A Standard is an attempt to resolve potential misunderstanding or disagreement. Communication protocols are one of many areas that standards may apply to. notable standards are not communication protocols, for, are the SI weight and measurement standards. These provide a fixed reference to can compare any given quantity to measure it in a way unambiguous to everyone with access to standard, or reasonable approximation. A Communication Protocol Standard is a formalization of rules of a communication protocol those with access to standard can unambiguously determine whether any attempt at communication complies with those rules. Just as comparing a particular mass of metal against SI standard kilogram will determine how close mass is to kilogram, comparing a particular protocol implementation against a protocol standard will determine whether it is truly following that protocol according to standard. When all parties are properly following the protocol as formalized in standard, it is, ideally guaranteed to result in level of communication that the protocol was designed to accommodate. A Communication Protocol Specification is a means by rules and formats of a communication protocol can be described at a formal level, it is often part of, largest part of a communication protocol standard. purpose of a standard is to create a means to determine whether something is truly an instance of the standardized thing, purpose of specification is to define exactly what the thing is in case where thing is defined by rules formats, as communication protocol is. An unambiguous definition of what something is can be used to create a new instance of thing and to determine whether an existing thing is an instance of thing being defined.a specification can be used as a standard, but being a standard also carries weight of social agreement value in complying with specification well enough for multiple implementations to assurance of working together. parties interested in this agreement work together to form a Standards Body in to define standards they will agree on for purpose of their desire to be to rely on compliance to a protocol. Without presence of this social agreement and standards body by standards are produced, protocol specifications aren't generally considered to constitute standards, though well-defined specifications have potential to be used as standards.

In practice, TCP easier to police in a firewalled network: Traffic pertaining to externally vs internally established connections, client vs server roles, can be clearly distinguished handled by separate policy. For example, can ensure hosts on protected network can access external web server but not to act as web server to outside clients. For UDP services (for example DNS), enforcing such policies requires more intelligence and guesswork, since to take information above and below transport layer into account.

TCP header (layer 4) doesn't have field for protocol number - protocol number is in IP header (layer 3). Layers 2 to 4 each encapsulate datagram of layer above inside headers for layer. Joanna Rutkowska, leader of Qubes project, does great job documenting concepts on Qubes is relying. I suggest you to get information at source, in read two following documents: Software compartmentalization vs. physical separation (Or why Qubes OS is more than just a random collection of VMs) How is Qubes OS different from. Qubes not brings user experience improvement compared to running several VMWare instance, but also brings more fine-grained isolation. To explain roughly, model describe is like putting set of smaller boxes (the VMs) inside a single big box (the host system). All VMs go through host system to access any device (network, USB, DVDs reader, etc. ), host system controls VMs, devices, user's interface and is directly facing Internet. idea behind Qubes is not to store small boxes into overpotent big box, but configure small boxes in a virtual local network so, together, they look like a big box without being one and without using one. need to look like something users already know is important for user's adoption. But behind scene all parts of system is meant isolated from each other. main differences are user interface not facing network and has no Internet connection. cron is a process deals with scheduled tasks whether logged in or not. not necessary to have screen or tmux session running since cron daemon execute scheduled tasks in separate shells. See man cron and man crontab for details.

launchd does more than cron. In to running programs at certain times, it can also run them based on other triggers: incoming network connection, when a file added to certain folder,. It can also relaunch a program if it crashes. If interested in it as replacement for cron, main difference is how it handles being asleep or shut down when a job is scheduled to run. In this case, cron doesn't run job, but launchd will notice a scheduled run missed, run it at next opportunity (although if missed multiple scheduled runs, it'll only run it once). Edit: point out things cron can do launchd cannot: automatic emailing of failure reports (you to write wrapper script to with launchd) and user-defined jobs that run even when user isn't logged in (a user can define launchd items in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, but they only run inside a login session).

By default, cron not log output of executed jobs. possible to log fact cronjobs executed, but not default on OS X either. In to investigate cronjob execution output, suggest modifying cronjob line to redirect STDOUT and STDERR to logfiles. In crontab file or after running crontab -e, add something like following to your job line: 0 0 * * * yourcommand >/tmp/stdout. log 2>/tmp/stderr. log Doing this should send STDOUT (normally printed or echo'ed output to STDOUT) to text file named stdout. log in /tmp directory, and STDERR to stderr. log in temp directory. Many utilities use STDERR to print special error messages out when're application errors, not errors generated by program's actual execution. (You read more about STDERR on Wikipedia. )

What is crl why Should it be revoked From RFC 3280 A certificate revocation list (CRL) is time-stamped listidentifying revoked certificates signed by a CA or CRL issuerand made freely available in publicrepository. Each revoked certificate is identified in CRL by itscertificate serial number. When certificate-using system uses a certificate (e., for verifying remote user's digital signature), system not checks certificate signatureand validity acquires a suitably recent CRL checks certificate serial number is not on that CRL. From RFC 5280 meaning of "suitably recent" may vary with local policy, but it usuallymeans most recently issued CRLA new CRL is issued on regular periodic basis (e., hourly, daily, or weekly). entryis added to CRL as part of next update following notification of revocation. entry MUST NOT be removed from CRL until it appears on one regularly scheduled CRL issued beyondthe revoked certificate's validity period. advantage of revocation method is CRLs may be distributed by same means as certificates, via untrusted servers and untrusted communications. CRl's would revoke when private key of asymmetric encryption key pair (whose public key certified by CA) is stolen. In situation, anybody with private key could decrypt all communication between user and certified entity. CRLs issued periodically, certificates expired may be tagged as revoked, or may be issued as soon as certificate is revoked. To keep CRLs from being faked, they are signed by public key of CA and contain timestamp, after which CRLs expire. Reasons for revocation : According to ietf common reasons for revocation were : keyCompromise CACompromise affiliationChanged superseded cessationOfOperation certificateHold removeFromCRL privilegeWithdrawn AACompromise Reference 2 Reference 3

fundamental things: basis of a CRL is a promise for a certain time period. means begin time and end time. Once CRL is made and signed, it can't be changed, it lasts as long as it lasts, and can't be trusted after that. In, you won't know until you check. A CRL in regular form is one big list. can't assume size is an indication. verifier needs to know exactly what Certificates are no longer trusted. need to get a fresh copy, either way. no protocol to check "is this same as my old one?" primary implementation of CRLs is not "go get one when you need it" but "get it ahead of time, and check it when you need to". primary mechanism of distribution is series of file downloads and caches. A server won't know next CRL is exactly the same as currently expiring CRL until it has both - at, if you have fresh version, why check? If needed is a "ask when you need it, you'll always have access" structure, then go with OSCP. basic rationale of validity dates is to allow PKI implementers to make conscious decision about how long to go with out checking in with CRL issuer. PKI system will make this decision on issuer by issuer basis, in accordance with risk to system and patterns of intended usage. real challenge - validity should be commensurate with risk - how long are system protectors willing to wait before checking in on "known bad guy" list? basic premise relate to looking at canned food in submarine. expiration date is how long manufacturer promises it'll be OK to consume it. Can you eat meat a day after expiration date? Yep. In, day-old meat is a better option than starving to death. What about meat 6 months past it's expiration date? Well.what kind of germs are you up against? real possibility this food will make you sicker than not eating anything (just shutting down doing no transactions until fresh CRL). In all cases, reality is, you weight cost of doing business against risk of uncertain data. NOTE: this applies only to general, garden variety CRL. number of alternate formats out there. Last I looked, they were all proprietary. but it been a while. some alternate formats can work differently, as they all aim at simplifying.

In X. 509 model, no restriction on download. When a verifier (say, a Web browser) wants to validate a certificate, it will try to obtain extra information through other objects: certificates, CRL. it may obtain these objects over insecure channels.'s point of CRL being signed: verifier will trust a CRL not because it just obtained it from specific Web site, but because CRL is signed by authorized CRL issuer (usually the CA itself). bright side of principle is it makes X. 509 certificates applicable to all kinds of networks. Otherwise, harsh chicken-and-egg problem: how would you trust you got right, most recent revocation information ? Because downloaded it from HTTPS server ? But how did verify certificate of that server ? so on. But dark side, of: a CRL is a snapshot of revocation information at a given date. Being signed, it is immutable. cannot be changed. always a bit stale. verifier will require CRL it uses are "not too old" --, implies regular publishing of newer CRL. On technical point of view, may envision specific kind of CRL which does not contain whole list of revoked certificates (which can be bulky) but only short message stating "no certificate revoked since that date", allowing to extend lifetime of a CRL. This exists; it called delta CRL. With delta CRL, new CRL is virtually emitted at regular intervals, without necessarily forcing download of new big file. Unfortunately, not all software know how to use delta CRL. Another technique is segmentation: split CRL into many smaller files, each talking about only a subset of certificates. Down road lie very small CRL which assert revocation status of only one certificate at a time; this known as OCSP., support is in deployment.

Unix system administrators use cron to schedule processes/jobs to run at certain intervals, this is likely what is happening here, and on many sites across net where actions like mailing list unsubscribe requests produce similar message saying certain amount time for process to be completed. Database operations can be "expensive" in time and processor power, as connection needs to be opened to DB, commands executed, returning information processed, finally connection needs to be closed. For time-sensitive operation like signing up for a site or service, provider usually opts to run these DB operations in real time, but other, less-sensitive operations may be scheduled to avoid excessive DB open/close requests.

After device status changes from “Pairing” to “Paired, ” AirPods are ready to use. Start playing music. steps from iDownloadBlog. According to support article from Apple Apple Watch Series 2 has Bluetooth 4. 0 chip. common bluetooth headphones should also work with Watch.

From apt-get manual: upgrade upgrade used to install newest versions of all packages currently installed on system from sources enumerated in /etc/apt/sources. list. See also apt_preferences(5) for mechanism for overriding general settings for individual packages.

a simple solution for getting your contacts at least. This what I did from one iPhone to another iPhone. Login to iCloud account associated with device you trying to retrieve this data from. Once logged in click on contacts tab in iCloud. In bottom left hand corner see "setting gear". Click this and then click select all. Once all selected, click "settings gear" and click export vcard. Save as contacts somewhere you to easily locate like your desktop. Log out of account and log into account you wish to transfer this data to. Once logged in to account, click contacts and "settings gear" in left hand corner. Click import vcard, locate and select vcard imported from other account. You should now see your contacts transferred from one account to next. then need to click "setting gear" again click refresh contacts. Power off your device associated with device you want contacts transferred and power back on. Once everything updated you should see your contacts on your new device. Best of luck!

" When you start working on a software development project you quickly discover development methodology used major part to in speed and quality of code developed. Since Agile methodology is widely used important you understand advantages and disadvantages of agile to determine it best fit for your project deliverables. Agile software development is a conceptual framework for undertaking software engineering projects. Most agile methods attempt to minimize risk by developing software in short timeboxes, called iterations, typically last one to four weeks. Each iteration is like a miniature software project of own, includes all of tasks necessary to release mini-increment of new functionality: planning, requirements analysis, design, coding, testing, documentation.'s good process for company because it include customer in development process make it responsible for product delivery. In other customers happy because they find theirs self participating in development of product. Demerits for Agile: Agile is too programmer-centric leaving unclear how to balance work across organization. If You Don't Know Where You're Going, Agile Won't Get You There! Creation of frameworks without clear needs. Overuse of language features (inappropriately). No test-first mentality. for interesting methodology might work as alternative for AGILE may be best viewed under these 3 links : Kanban as Alternative Agile Implementation Kanban software development Lean software development on the cloud

Incremental Approach uses set number of steps development goes from start to finish in linear path of progression. Incremental development done in steps from design, implementation, testing/verification, maintenance. can be broken down further into sub-steps but most incremental models follow same pattern. Waterfall Model is traditional incremental development approach. Iterative Approach has no set number of steps, development is done in cycles. Iterative development less concerned with tracking progress of individual features. Instead, focus is put on creating working prototype first adding features in development cycles where Increment Development steps done for every cycle. Agile Modeling is typical iterative approach. incremental model originally developed to follow traditional assembly line model used in factories., software design and development has little in common with manufacturing physical goods. Code is blueprint not finished product of development. Good design choices often 'discovered' during development process. Locking developers into assumptions without proper context may lead to poor designs in best case or complete derailing of development in worst. iterative approach now becoming common practice because better fits natural path of progression in software development. Instead of investing time/effort chasing 'perfect design' based on assumptions, iterative approach is all about creating something's 'good enough' to start and evolving it to fit user's needs. tl;dr - If you writing essay under Incremental Model, you'd attempt to write it perfectly from start to finish one sentence at at time. If wrote it under Iterative Model, you'd bang out quick rough draft work to improve it through set of revision phases. Update: modified definition for 'Incremental Approach' to fit more practical example. If had to deal with contracting Incremental Approach is how most contracts are carried out (especially for military). Despite many subtle variations of typical 'Waterfall Model' most/all of are applied the same way in practice.steps go follows: Contract Award Preliminary Design Review Critical Design Review Specification Freeze Development Fielding/Integration Verification Reliability Testing PDR and CDR are where spec is created and revised. Once spec is complete, it should be frozen to prevent scope creep. Integration occurs if software used to extend pre-existing system. Verification is for checking application matches spec. Reliability is a test to prove application reliable over long term, can be specified like a SLA (Service Level Agreement) where system required to sustain certain percentage of uptime (ex 99% uptime for 3 months). model works great for systems straightforward to specify on paper but difficult to produce. Software is difficult to specify on paper to appreciable degree of detail (ex UML). Most 'business types' in charge of management/contracting fail to realize software development -- code itself is the spec. Paper specifications often take as much or more time/effort to write as code itself usually prove to be incomplete/inferior in practice. Incremental approaches attempt to wasted time/resources by treating code itself as specification. Instead of running paper spec through multiple revision steps, code itself goes through multiple cycles of revision.

Wikipedia lists these as methodologies/development processes: Agile - based on iterative and incremental development, requirements and solutions evolve through collaboration between self-organizing, cross-functional teams. Agile Modeling is typical iterative approach. incremental model originally developed to follow traditional assembly line model used in factories., software design and development has little in common with manufacturing physical goods. Once spec is complete, it should be frozen to prevent scope creep. Integration occurs if software used to extend pre-existing system. Verification is for checking application matches spec. Software is difficult to specify on paper to appreciable degree of detail (ex UML). Instead of running paper spec through multiple revision steps, code itself goes through multiple cycles of revision.

V-model is an extension of Waterfall model, don't expect it to be hugely different. Basically, you follow V-model from left to right, just like in Waterfall model. In Waterfall, you do requirements, design, implementation, verification and finally maintenance. In same way, in V-model, you do requirements, design, implementation, verification and maintenance: same steps in both cases. major differences with Waterfall are way it presented and emphasis on testing. Representing flow as V-shape helps making difference between everything prior to coding (requirements, architecture and design) and everything follows coding (essentially testing). While tests are just one of five steps in Waterfall, looks like practically half of process in V-model. diagram in question is more complicated. tries to show, for example, system design step leads not only to system design document, like Waterfall model suggest, but also system tests design, will later help writing system tests. diagram puts more emphasis on testing., doing system test design helps in architecture design (it be awkward to do architecture design regardless system test design). Searching other explanations on internet, can't avoid quoting following article by Bhakti Satalkar: main difference between waterfall model and V model is in waterfall model, testing activities are carried out after development activities are over. On in V model, testing activities start with first stage itself. In, waterfall model is a continuous process, while V model is a simultaneous process. As compared to software made using waterfall model, number of defects in software made using V model are less. due to fact, testing activities, carried out simultaneously in V model. Therefore, waterfall model is used, when requirements of user are fixed. If requirements of user are uncertain and keep changing, then V model is better alternative. This explanation is misleading. true only if you replace “V-model” in quote by any Agile method.Unlike article states, in V-model, testing done after coding; for example, see Wikipedia: common practical criticism of V-Model is it leads to testing squeezed into tight windows at end of development when earlier stages overrun but implementation date remains fixed., in V-model, system test design follows system design without waiting until product implementation done, doesn't mean tests performed before coding. author confounds V-model with Agile approaches like Test Driven Development (TDD) in Extreme Programming (XP).

RSTP mapped to PVST+ VLAN 1 instance, make sure you have VLAN 1 enabled on any trunks between RSTP and PVST+ regions for two to interoperate., if PVST+ regions separated by RSTP region, PVST+ BPDUs are transparently forwarded across RSTP region (so long as VLANs are trunked), RSTP region acts like a shared network interconnecting PVST+ regions.

possible to mix PVST and MST (RSTP requires MST), but needs planning, and can be fragile, as you discovered. better off using same STP version across all your switches. You could change STP on Cisco switches to match rest of switches. Cisco has several documents about how to interoperate with non-Cisco switches (e. g. Understanding Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol), or how to convert Cisco switches to MST (e. g. Configuration example to migrate Spanning Tree from PVST+ to MST). also lot of other documents about this subject, you will find if do Google search.

Yes. protocol no longer secure, cracking initial MS-CHAPv2 authentication can be reduced to difficulty of cracking a single DES 56-bit key, with current computers can be brute-forced in short time (making strong password irrelevant to security of PPTP as entire 56-bit keyspace can be searched within practical time constraints). attacker can do MITM to capture handshake (and any PPTP traffic after), do offline crack of handshake and derive RC4 key. Then, attacker will able to decrypt and analyse traffic carried in PPTP VPN. PPTP not provide forward secrecy, just cracking one PPTP session is sufficient to crack all previous PPTP sessions using same credentials., PPTP provides weak protection to integrity of data being tunneled. RC4 cipher, while providing encryption, does not verify integrity of data not an Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) cipher. PPTP doesn't do additional integrity checks on traffic (such as HMAC), vulnerable to bit-flipping attacks,. attacker can modify PPTP packets with little possibility of detection. Various discovered attacks on RC4 cipher (such as Royal Holloway attack) make RC4 a bad choice for securing large amounts of transmitted data, VPNs are prime candidate for such attacks as they by nature usually transmit sensitive and large amounts of data. If want to, you can try cracking a PPTP session yourself. For Wi-Fi user, it involves ARP poisoning target target sends MSCHAPv2 handshake through you (which you can capture with Wireshark or any other packet capture tool). You can then crack handshake with tools like Chap2Asleap, or if few hundred dollars to spare submit captured handshake to online cracking services.recovered username, hash, password encryption keys can used to impersonate logins to VPN, or retroactively decrypt target's traffic., please do not do this without proper authorisation outside controlled environment., avoid using PPTP where possible. For more information, see http://www. computerworld. com/s/article/9229757/Tools_released_at_Defcon_can_crack_widely_used_PPTP_encryption_in_under_a_day How can I tell if PPTP tunnel is secure?. Issues discovered with RC4 in real world security issues in protocols like TLS) found in http://www. isg. rhul. ac. uk/tls/RC4mustdie. html https://www. rc4nomore. com/ For cracking portion, refer to https://www. rastating. com/cracking-pptp-ms-chapv2-with-chapcrack-cloudcracker/ https://samsclass. info/124/proj14/p10-pptp. htm.

SFTP isn't FTP protocol over ssh, but extension to SSH protocol included in SSH2 (and some SSH1 implementations). SFTP is file transfer protocol similar to FTP uses SSH protocol as network protocol benefits from leaving SSH to handle authentication and encryption). SCP only for transferring files, can't do other things like list remote directories or removing files, SFTP does do. FISH appears another protocol can use either SSH or RSH to transfer files. UPDATE (2021/03/09): to release notes of OpenSSH 8. 0/8. 0p1 (2019-04-17): scp protocol outdated, inflexible not readily fixed. recommend use of modern protocols like sftp and rsync for file transfer instead.

FISH and SFTP similar, observed do both work over SSH, SFTP requires specific support and configuration in SSH Server to facilitate transfer, but it bit more secure allows for SysAdmins to only allow SFTP (in these situations FISH won't work). FISH requires shell (sh/rsh for instance) to copy, requires full SSH access to machine, imagine it harder to secure (I cannot comment objectively as I've never had to). Where possible,'d recommend SFTP, scp, FISH (in that order). Wikipedia FISH Article

Delete the shorter track Return to iTunes and delete the short version of track, remembering to check length carefully before do so. Finally go to bottom right hand corner and click Apply. Set new ringtone All remains to be done now is to go to Settings on iPhone, then Sounds, and'll find new ringtone at top of list. Simply put, an ADT (Abstract Data Type) is logical description, a Data Structure is concrete. Think of an ADT as a picture of data and operations to manipulate change it. A Data Structure is real, concrete thing. It can be implemented and used within algorithm.
ADT is interface (what it does) a data structure is class (how it does it). few examples: ADT: List DS: ArrayList, LinkedList. ADT: Map DS: HashMap, TreeMap. guess you get the point.

Abstract Data Type: ADT may be defined as a set of data values and associated operations precisely specified independent of implementation. an Abstract Data Type is an organized collection of information and a set of operations to manage information. The set of operations defines interface of ADT. as ADT fulfills conditions of interface, it doesn’t matter how ADT is implemented., in ADT, data values and operations are defined with mathematical precision, rather than as implementation in computer language, we may reason about effects of operations, relations to other abstract data types whether program implements data type etc. simplest abstract data type is the stack data type for functions might be provided to create empty stack, to push values onto a stack and pop values from a stack. basic difference between abstract data type (ADT) and concrete data type is latter allow us to look at concrete representation, former hide representation from us. An ADT may be pure ADT or Updatable ADT. A pure ADT is one where all operations are pure functions. means operations have no side effects. In, they do not modify or update input arguments. They just use these arguments to generate output, are fresh values of ADT (or of other types). Most concrete types are pure. For example, no operation on integers modifies an integer. Instead, all operations like ‘+’ produce fresh outputs. An updatable ADT is one where some operations change values of ADT. For example, suppose operation called ‘pop’ that took a stack as argument modified it., “destructively”) by removing highest priority item. This operation would be considered impure and whole ADT would be impure also. An ADT may be user defined ADT. an Abstract Data Type is a data type that satisfies following two conditions: representation, or definition, of type and operations are contained in a single syntactic unit.representation of objects of type is hidden from program units use type, only direct operations possible on objects are provided in type’s definition. user defined Abstract Data Type should provide: type definition that allows program units to declare variables of type, but hides representation of these variables. set of operations for manipulating objects of type. example of user defined abstract data type is structure. ’C’ provides four basic types: int, char, float and double., ‘C’ also provides programmer ability to define his/her own types. Structure is one such example. structure is an aggregate of different parts, each part is of some existing type. struct abc {int x; float y; }; above structure definition does not create variables, rather creates new type. Variables of this type may be created in similar way to variables of built in type. struct abc a; typedef keyword allows to create new type names for new types. For example: typedef struct abc AB; where AB is new type name can now be used to create new types. AB b; Data Structures: characteristic features of data structures: contains component data items, may be atomic or another data structure (still domain). set of operations on one or more of component items. Defines rules as to how components relates to each other and to structure as a whole (assertions). Data Structures: data structure may be static or dynamic. static data structure has fixed size. meaning different from meaning of static modifier. Arrays are static; once define number of elements can hold, number doesn’t change. dynamic data structure grows and shrinks at execution time as required by contents. dynamic data structure implemented using links. Data structures may be categorized into linear data structures and non-linear data structures.In linear data structures every component has unique predecessor successor, except first and last elements, in non-linear data structures, no such restriction as elements may be arranged in any desired fashion restricted by way we use to represent such types.

First, Terminologies in data Structures can be confusing. ADT is like theory or model guideline. tells how a data structure should behave, operations it should support. Three fundamental abstract data types are containers, dictionaries, priority queues. For example dictionary, tells us every data structure implements this dictionary ADT must support key-value pairs, search based on keys, insertion of items, finding successor and predecessor of given key. everything else implements this above ADT is Data structure (DS), Data structure are real things you implement in problems find inside libraries. In case of dictionary, you can chose to implement it via Array or Linked list. real confusion arises when someone name their DS as ADT, for example some people will call DS as 'Dictionary' instead of DictImplementation is perfectly legal, causes confusion. Ref: Skiena : The algorithm design manual

UAT environment set up for "user acceptance" of new functionality. to test functionality, QA or stakeholders may set up user profiles particular way to exercise particular features, or may set up mock products or configurations to check them all out. staging environment is often set up with copy of production data, sometimes anonymized. Some corporations regularly "refresh" staging database from production snapshot. primary focus is to ensure application will work in production same way it worked in UAT. Instead of setting up data anew, testers will search database for profiles and products that match essential set of test cases. Often "real" data have quirks give rise to unexpected edge cases missed during UAT., any data migration testing need to take place in staging environment.

Inline Data Attribute records store small attributes can fit within record itself. Fork Data Attribute records contain references to maximum of eight extents can hold larger attributes. Extension Attributes used to extend Fork Data Attribute record when its eight extent records are already used. You copying a file to a block device. consider the two. A file is usually stored in a file system. file broken up to equal size blocks generally stored non contiguously. file system contains a table links blocks together. Block devices also contain equal sized blocks. When block device is an a physical device, a USB flash drive, these blocks are stored contiguously. Since blocks are contiguous, no need for a table containing links., virtual block devices are not physical devices, but are actually files themselves. Stored in these files is all information needed to represent a physical block device., these files may contain additional information needed to describe physical device. An iso file is this type of file. Block devices generally contain a table define contiguous blocks called partitions. Not all block devices have such tables. File systems usually stored in these partitions., not all files systems require a partition container and partitions do not contain file systems exclusively. Initially, 16GB USB flash drive contained a partition table. This table had entry allowed for FAT formatted file system to reside contiguously on most (if not all) of remaining blocks. command you entered overwrote this partition table and partially overwrote file system. In, iso file copied sequentially to flash drive starting first block of drive. end result?, disk utility (actually macOS) thinks at least one partition on USB drive this partition should contain a Windows_FAT_32 file system. Of, this is wrong, but this what was interpreted from results of your dd command.

gpt is a tool to edit GUID partition table of a disk. It only modifies primary and secondary GPT header and table and MBR. Or with it only modifies first 34 blocks and last 33 blocks of a device. means if you add a partition starting at block 40 and ending at block 409640 (these boundaries of typical OS X EFI partition) it doesn't write anything to blocks 40-409640 but only to GPT headers/tables. Adding a partition doesn't result in file system less in readable file system. To create a file system you to format partition with appropriate tool like newfs_hfs! After formatting partition file system is essentially empty except necessary parts "represent" file system like catalog file, allocation file etc. If you remove a partition with file system or remove whole partition table containing several formatted partitions with gpt remove|destroy. file system(s) won't be touched. after restoring a partition or partition table with same values previously file system(s) with all content will "reappear". One (rare) case exists where partition might be enlarged: if unallocated disk space is directly "behind" a partition. If you first remove a partition with gpt and then re-add partition with same start block but larger size previous file system is completely in boundaries of new partition. But at least allocation file (~volume bitmap) is corrupted and alternative volume header is at wrong location. Usually such "intentionally corrupted" file system can be repaired with diskutil repairVolume. highly discouraged though to use this method to enlarge a partition. Modifying disk partitions with gpt like in will delete any current partition (and its content) with high probability.resize (expand shrink) current partition keeping content use diskutil!
