Simply put, an ADT (Abstract Data Type) is logical description, a Data Structure is concrete. Think of an ADT as a picture of data and operations to manipulate change it. A Data Structure is real, concrete thing. It can be implemented and used within algorithm.
ADT is interface (what it does) a data structure is class (how it does it). few examples: ADT: List DS: ArrayList, LinkedList. ADT: Map DS: HashMap, TreeMap. guess you get the point.

Abstract Data Type: ADT may be defined as a set of data values and associated operations precisely specified independent of implementation. an Abstract Data Type is an organized collection of information and a set of operations to manage information. The set of operations defines interface of ADT. as ADT fulfills conditions of interface, it doesn’t matter how ADT is implemented., in ADT, data values and operations are defined with mathematical precision, rather than as implementation in computer language, we may reason about effects of operations, relations to other abstract data types whether program implements data type etc. simplest abstract data type is the stack data type for functions might be provided to create empty stack, to push values onto a stack and pop values from a stack. basic difference between abstract data type (ADT) and concrete data type is latter allow us to look at concrete representation, former hide representation from us. An ADT may be pure ADT or Updatable ADT. A pure ADT is one where all operations are pure functions. means operations have no side effects. In, they do not modify or update input arguments. They just use these arguments to generate output, are fresh values of ADT (or of other types). Most concrete types are pure. For example, no operation on integers modifies an integer. Instead, all operations like ‘+’ produce fresh outputs. An updatable ADT is one where some operations change values of ADT. For example, suppose operation called ‘pop’ that took a stack as argument modified it., “destructively”) by removing highest priority item. This operation would be considered impure and whole ADT would be impure also. An ADT may be user defined ADT. an Abstract Data Type is a data type that satisfies following two conditions: representation, or definition, of type and operations are contained in a single syntactic unit.representation of objects of type is hidden from program units use type, only direct operations possible on objects are provided in type’s definition. user defined Abstract Data Type should provide: type definition that allows program units to declare variables of type, but hides representation of these variables. set of operations for manipulating objects of type. example of user defined abstract data type is structure. ’C’ provides four basic types: int, char, float and double., ‘C’ also provides programmer ability to define his/her own types. Structure is one such example. structure is an aggregate of different parts, each part is of some existing type. struct abc {int x; float y; }; above structure definition does not create variables, rather creates new type. Variables of this type may be created in similar way to variables of built in type. struct abc a; typedef keyword allows to create new type names for new types. For example: typedef struct abc AB; where AB is new type name can now be used to create new types. AB b; Data Structures: characteristic features of data structures: contains component data items, may be atomic or another data structure (still domain). set of operations on one or more of component items. Defines rules as to how components relates to each other and to structure as a whole (assertions). Data Structures: data structure may be static or dynamic. static data structure has fixed size. meaning different from meaning of static modifier. Arrays are static; once define number of elements can hold, number doesn’t change. dynamic data structure grows and shrinks at execution time as required by contents. dynamic data structure implemented using links. Data structures may be categorized into linear data structures and non-linear data structures.In linear data structures every component has unique predecessor successor, except first and last elements, in non-linear data structures, no such restriction as elements may be arranged in any desired fashion restricted by way we use to represent such types.

First, Terminologies in data Structures can be confusing. ADT is like theory or model guideline. tells how a data structure should behave, operations it should support. Three fundamental abstract data types are containers, dictionaries, priority queues. For example dictionary, tells us every data structure implements this dictionary ADT must support key-value pairs, search based on keys, insertion of items, finding successor and predecessor of given key. everything else implements this above ADT is Data structure (DS), Data structure are real things you implement in problems find inside libraries. In case of dictionary, you can chose to implement it via Array or Linked list. real confusion arises when someone name their DS as ADT, for example some people will call DS as 'Dictionary' instead of DictImplementation is perfectly legal, causes confusion. Ref: Skiena : The algorithm design manual

Confusion arises from relationship between these concepts is complex changed over time. In current systems difference between a named fork and extended attribute is largely academic. For extended attribute, actual data is stored in attribute data record. For a fork,'s stored is the list of disk allocation blocks contain data. A resource fork is still a fork. Basic file system metadata is stored in dedicated elements of file system record itself, independent of attributes and named fork references.

top enables to see processes ordered by processor power they use. ps enables see all processes, or just processes used by certain users, for example root or yourself. top should be used to see processes most active, ps could used to see processes you (or any other user) running currently. for more information about how to use top and ps, run man top or man ps in terminal ;)

top display as many columns as width of window allow. to change sort to cpu (high to low), can type following within top: o to select primary sort -cpu to sort by decreasing CPU usage add secondary sort if desired: O to select secondary sort -mem to sort by decreasing memory usage ? will show all options, with current sort selections - see below image: can also call these options explicitly from command line, if desired, like this: To see longest running processes top -o time -user $(whoami)

JOIN and INNER JOIN same, inner keyword optional as all joins considered to be inner joins unless otherwise specified. difference between JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN same as difference between INNER JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN. INNER JOIN only return matched rows if a row in table A matches many rows in table B table A row repeated with each table B row and vice versa. FULL OUTER JOIN return everything inner join does and return all unmatched rows from each table.
database relationship usually has 2 tables linked together. One table (the "belongs to"-side) contains foreign key to other table "has many"-side). most relations have both sides.

has many Useful for describing 1:n or n:n relationships. Using 1:n relationship, looking at single object and looking at 1 or more other objects related to first object. A parking garage has many cars parked. primary object has many secondary objects. primary key has many foreign keys (linking primary entry to many other entries in other tables. ) belongs to Useful for describing 1:1 or n:1 relationships (note n:1 is reverse of 1:n, looking at relationship in opposite direction. ) A car belongs to parking garage. secondary object belongs to primary object. In n:n case: foreign key is referenced by / belongs to primary key.

http://www. differencebetween. com/difference-between-api-and-vs-sdk/ What is API? API is an interface allows software programs to interact with each other. It defines set of rules be followed by programs to communicate with other. APIs specify how routines, data structures,. should be defined in for two applications to communicate. APIs differ in the functionality provided by. are general APIs provide library functionalities of a programming language such as Java API. also APIs provides specific functionalities such as Google Maps API. also language dependent APIs, only be used by a specific programming language., language independent APIs could be used with several programming languages. APIs needs to be implemented carefully by exposing only required functionality or data to outside, while keeping the other parts of application inaccessible. Usage of APIs has become popular in internet. It common to allow some of functionality and data through an API to the outside on the Web. This functionality can be combined to offer improved functionality to users. What is SDK? SDK is a set of tools be used to develop software applications targeting a specific platform. SDKs include tools, libraries, documentation and sample code help programmer to develop application. Most of SDKs could be downloaded from the internet and many the SDKs are provided free to encourage programmers to use SDK‘s programming language. Some widely used SDKs are Java SDK (JDK) includes all libraries, debugging utilities, etc., make writing programs easier in Java. SDKs make life of a software developer easy, since no need to look for components/ tools compatible with each other and all are integrated in to a single package is easy to install. What is the difference between API and SDK? API is an interface allows software programs to interact with each other, a SDK is a set of tools can be used to develop software applications targeting a specific platform.simplest version of a SDK could be API contains files required to interact with a specific programming language. So an API can be seen as simple SDK without debugging support, etc.

If mean should use a router to connect two separate switches to each other at Layer 2 probably not no. router designed to be a gateway between two different layer two domains rather than linking them at Layer 2. If want VLAN on each switch to single VLAN spanning both switches connect them to each other. If want to use same VLAN ID to provide two separate VLANs, one on each switch, with different subnets assigned, then sure go via router., can often make router bridge two interfaces together, effectively making router ports "switch", as switches are just bridging. In Cisco land, call this integrated routing and bridging.

A VLAN is Ethernet level concept, a subnet is IP level concept. VLAN splits Ethernet network into multiple logically seperate Ethernet networks. subnet defines which hosts host will try to communicate with directly verses which hosts need to go via a router. It also defines "network" and "broadcast" addresses. common practice to have 1:1 mapping between subnets and VLANs but possible to have multiple subnets on same VLAN. possible to use proxy arp to split a subnet between multiple VLANs or have two VLANs using same IP subnet for different purposes.

Vlan is broadcast domain. default hosts in single Vlan communicates each other. different Vlans won't communicate each other, ensure communication between different Vlans host routing between Vlans mandatory for Configuring routing between Vlan layer3 device required. inter-Vlan routing or using layer3 device SVi can be configured with different Vlans make them talk to each.

Two separate VLANs must communicate through a layer-3 device, like a router. Devices on a VLAN communicate with each other using layer-2. Layer-3 must used to communicate between separate layer-2 domains. Assuming most common communications (layer-2 is ethernet and layer-3 is IP), when a host on a VLAN wants to communicate with another host on same VLAN, it discovers other hosts layer-2 (e. g. MAC) address with like ARP, sends frame to MAC address. When a host on one VLAN wants to send something to host on another VLAN, it must use a layer-3 (e. g. IP) address. host use layer-2 to send frames to its defined gateway (router). router will strip off layer-2 frame inspect layer-3 packet for destination layer-3 address. router will then look up next hop for layer-3 address. create a new layer-2 frame for layer-3 packet based on layer-2 LAN on interface where it needs to send packet for next hop. Other routers in path to end LAN repeat this process until frame is placed on final VLAN, where receiving host gets the frame. You search for the OSI model and learn how it works. remember it is a model, some things in real world don't necessarily work exactly like model predict, but it will give gross understanding of how data travel from application on one host to application on another host.

In many implementations IPv4 subnet and a VLAN closely correlated on 1:1 basis. A subnet, is a portion of IPv4 address space from may assign addresses to hosts. differentiated from a "prefix" a term in common parlance or a supernet, may be a larger portion of IP address space comprised of many subnets. reason for correlation is a single VLAN and single subnet both represent a single broadcast domain., these two tend to be overlaid in most implementations. described in earlier answers, a VLAN is a layer 2 entity. All hosts on given VLAN can communicate with each other, but no hosts on one VLAN can communicate to hosts on another without form routing or in rare cases, bridging.

native VLAN only relevant to 802. 1q, yes it untagged by default, but can be tagged if required. Ports assigned to native VLAN if no other config present. It's ok to keep it as VLAN 1, but can be changed, to remember to shut down unused ports. by, if I plugged my evil hacker laptop into working port left as VLAN 1, I could potentially be to span across your entire network, whereas you could change native VLAN to VLAN 10, and then not assign VLAN 10 to any ports. ISL has no concept of native VLAN.

no reason not to put multiple subnets on same VLAN, but also probably no reason to do it. Pro: Allows subnets to talk directly without router or firewall Save's VLANs Con: Allows subnets to talk directly without router or firewall It's messy from documentation and troubleshooting perspective More broadcast traffic We generally don't do it because of messiness and lack of security. One VLAN = one subnet is easier to document and easier to troubleshoot usually not good reason to complicate things. only reason of to do it is company mergers or network upgrades for both prefer it to be temporary. Edit to clarify, for hosts on different subnets same VLAN to talk directly need to either make them their own default gateway or add route to "other" subnet that connects it to interface. In gateway case if host IP was 10. 1. 1. 2 then gateway would also be 10. 1. 1. 2. This cause host to ARP for everything on or off it's subnet. allow it to talk to second subnet on VLAN but only way able to talk to anything else is if router/firewall running proxy arp can help it out. In route out interface case add something like "route add -net 192. 56. 76. 0 netmask 255. 255. 255. 0 eth0" to device then 10. 1. 1. 2 will ARP directly on eth0 when it wants to reach 192. 56. 76. *.

Source or Destination MAC address not to be unique across different VLANs., can not create correlation between MAC address of frame and VLAN frame should be in. Take First Hop Redundancy Protocols (HSRP/VRRP), for example. could have a pair of L3 switches doing HSRP/VRRP for five different VLANs. If each VLAN uses same VRRP ID# each VRRP Gateway IP address will share same MAC address (00-00-5E-00-01-<ID#>). exact same MAC address in five different VLANs. reason need VLAN Tagging is to distinguish VLAN traffic on port where multiple VLANs can exist. access port is port carries traffic for only one VLAN. Trunk port is port carries traffic for multiple VLANs. On Trunk ports, all frames are still carried across wire in form of 1s and 0s. Something has to exist in for sending switch to indicate to receiving switch which 1s and 0s belong to which VLAN. That something is a VLAN Tag. VLAN Tag added whenever frame crossing trunk port and removed when other switch receives frame. egrep is 100% equivalent to grep -E fgrep is 100% equivalent to grep -F Historically these switches provided in separate binaries. On some old Unix systems need to call separate binaries, but on all modern systems switches preferred. man page for grep has details about this. for, -E switches grep into a special mode so expression evaluated as an ERE (Extended Regular Expression) as opposed to normal pattern matching. Details of syntax on man page. -E, --extended-regexp Interpret PATTERN as an extended regular expression -F switch switches grep into a different mode it accepts a pattern to match, but splits pattern up into one search string per line and does OR search on any strings without special pattern matching. -F, --fixed-strings Interpret PATTERN as a list of fixed strings, separated by newlines, any of which is to be matched. example scenarios: You have a file with list of say ten Unix usernames in plain text. want to search group file on machine to see if any of ten users listed are in any special groups: grep -F -f user_list. txt /etc/group -F switch helps is usernames in pattern file interpreted as plain text strings. Dots for example interpreted as dots rather than wild-cards. want to search using fancy expression. For example parenthesis () can be used to indicate groups with | used as an OR operator. could run this search using -E: grep -E '^no(fork|group)' /etc/group. to return lines that start with either "nofork" or "nogroup". Without -E switch to escape special characters involved because with normal pattern matching they would just search for exact pattern; grep '^no\(fork\|group\)' /etc/group

┌── ln(1) link, ln -- make links │ Create symbolic link. │ optional path to intended symlink │ if omitted, symlink. named as destination can use. or ~ or other relative paths │ ┌─────┴────────┐ ln -s /path/to/original /path/to/symlink └───────┬───────┘ └── path to original file/folder can use. or ~ or other relative paths $ echo content > original $ ln -s original symlink $ ls -la original symlink -rw-r--r-- 1 grgarside staff 8 28 Jan 18:44 original lrwxr-xr-x 1 grgarside staff 8 28 Jan 18:44 symlink -> original $ cat symlink content For more information about ln(1) see man page. path to symlink optional; if omitted, ln defaults to making link with same name as destination, in current directory: $ cd ~/Documents $ ln -s. /Pictures $ ls -l Pictures lrwxr-xr-x 1 user staff 11 Feb 1 17:05 Pictures ->. /Pictures To create symlink to replace system directory (e. if /Users pointing to another disk drive), need to disable System Integrity Protection. re-enable after symlink set up.

A symbolic link is a small file contains location (i. path and filename) of a target file, with a flag in directory entry indicating it's a symlink. When you open a symlink, the OS will follow location to find target file. If target is a symlink, it follows its location (1)(2) until location points to a file's not a symlink (let it the FinalFile). Then OS obtains inode of FinalFile (the inode contains metadata like modification-time and has a pointer to file's data). Finally inode of FinalFile is opened. From now on process uses that inode to read/write to the file. As changing symlink name or path, deleting the symlink, changing path or name of FinalFile or even deleting FinalFile(3) has no effect on process; it's still reading from the same inode. In most cases file-data operations on the symlink will affect the FinalFile (e. reading and writing to the symlink will read from/write to FinalFile) but exceptions: readlink() system call reads contents of symlink itself. File-metadata operations (like rename or delete) on will usually affect the symlink. But exceptions here: lstat() system call is like stat(), except it returns information on symlink itself rather than on FinalFile(2). (1)'s a limit on number of levels and things get more complex if location in symlink is a relative path. (2) Read symlink(7): symbolic link handling for more details. man 7 symlink (3) The rm command or unlink() system call doesn't physically remove a file. It removes the directory entry that points to inode of file. file itself is removed only if a) no more directory entries (hard links) that refer to its inode and b) no process has the file open.

Both hard links and symbolic links link a path to destination, substantial difference should be aware of: Hard links link a path to a file. This means if you rename/move destination file, hard link follows. Symbolic links link a path to a path. This means if you rename/move destination file, link is broken., later replacing file with different one will make link work again. Links of both types are made with ln tool. Hard links made without options, whereas symlinks made with -s option. For more information on constructing command, see: How can I create a symbolic link in Terminal?

Symlinks are a Unix concept. They special files point to other files, so, in many cases, accessing symlink (for instance if it points to shell script) really access underlying file (running script). Aliases are a Mac concept (though OS/2 had something similar, forget what it called). I can tell aliases can be made only from finder whereas symbolic links can be made from terminal window. (It possible to make an alias from command line but have to write applescript to do). Aliases have one advantage over symbolic links. If underlying file alias points to is moved alias is automatically updated. Not so with symbolic links; they break (i. e. point to nowhere) if underlying file is moved. symlink points to name of real file (inode) in file system. When system resolves symlink to find actual file and open it, it finds and uses the file's inode. At point, the path you used to get to file doesn't matter. OS doesn't cache, it reads from file by its inode. You could, understand, start reading file through hard link and remove hard link (as long as file is still linked from somewhere else), and it wouldn't cause problems as long as file has been resolved (name string->inode).

Synchronization is process of ensuring your iTunes and iPad/iPhone contain same up-to-date files. If you add, change, or delete a file from one location, synchronization process will add, change, or delete same file at other location. For example, if you had a few songs on your computer, and a few on your phone, ones on phone not on computer, ones on computer not on phone, then after a "sync" operation, contents of your computer AND phone is combination of contents of both devices., content on device 1 now exists on device 2 alongside device 2's original content, content of device 2 now exists on device 1 alongside device 1's original content.

Mail talks to mail server to show you messages. Only IMAP accounts can be synchronized as formal way for server and mail client on your mac to double check all messages to make sure everything in sync between two. Get mail focuses on Inbox relies on Mail app having "correct" view matching data on mail server. Synchronize allows for noise/errors/lost messages, incorrect statuses other real life bumps and errors. It double counts and double checks each every message to make sure things 100% correct. Synchronize also checks all folders recursively to get everything accounted for - not just subset of folders marked as having new mail. more "deep cleaning" be if you told mail to rebuild account or mailbox. means local storage mail uses on your mac has problems getting mail or synchronizing. It's last step before deleting account and starting over to download things cleanly from server. In - synchronize should normally do nothing - but it will fill in gaps as needed. (of course it will get new mail as part of total synchronization - but it's to be slower and use more resources on mac than just asking for new mail)

Synchronization is process of ensuring your iTunes and iPad/iPhone contain same up-to-date files. If you add, change, or delete a file from one location, synchronization process will add, change, or delete same file at other location. For example, if you had a few songs on your computer, and a few on your phone, ones on phone not on computer, ones on computer not on phone, then after a "sync" operation, contents of your computer AND phone is combination of contents of both devices., content on device 1 now exists on device 2 alongside device 2's original content, content of device 2 now exists on device 1 alongside device 1's original content.

virtual machines get same IP address from DHCP service long they have same Ethernet MAC address (a hardware address, unique like fingerprint, set by hardware manufacturer of network device). you running virtual machines, they have virtual hardware and they "fake" the MAC address. sure no two machines have same Ethernet hardware address. set Ethernet MAC address of virtual machine in VirtualBox in hardware network section (it looks like this: 3c:08:51:05:24:8a) check it in your running VM: sudo ifconfig en0: flags=8863<UP, BROADCAST, SMART, RUNNING, SIMPLEX, MULTICAST> mtu 1500 options=2b<RXCSUM, TXCSUM, VLAN_HWTAGGING, TSO4> ether 3c:08:51:05:24:8a media: autoselect (none) status: inactive

First of, it possible (especially for owner of hotel) to edit CCTV footage. However, I don't think this was the case. In, you haven't yet seen CCTV footage and you just relied on what security personnel told you.,'s more likely owner disabled CCTV cameras, than he edited footage during or after theft. Note he can technically disable them, since internal cameras not usually connected to police control room, nor to security company's one., my answer to 1) would be: he asked someone to turn off cameras, then entered your room (or sent someone else to do it). This option not easier to technically implement, but's also easier to get away with. In, should police step in and ask owner to show them footage, he could say cameras were down for error or for maintenance. If he was "smart" enough to keep cameras down for extended period of time before and after theft, he could get away with it. On other, police could spot something suspicious in tampered footage and continue investigation. In case, bottom line to 1) is: anyone having complete physical access to security system is able to do anything to it. This is variation of one of Ten Immutable Laws of Security (https://technet. microsoft. com/en-us/library/hh278941. aspx), usually applies to computers and computer networks, but holds for any kind of security system. By, you said "There was only one way of entry through door". This most likely not true, unless your room has no windows. However, if you didn't let windows open before leaving room or if windows weren't broken or tampered with, this option can be ruled out. You also asked: 2) How can I check if CCTV or recording's were tampered with? This is very difficult., if owner disabled CCTV cameras, there nothing you can do, as will be nothing to check.If he didn't, you could theoretically check for video tampering, but you should have: a) permission from owner to have at least a copy of footage on a DVD; AND b) technical skills and tools to analyze footage. it's not easy to analyze a video and check if it been tampered with. As example, look at technologies used by the FBI in to do this analysis: https://archives. fbi. gov/archives/about-us/lab/forensic-science-communications/fsc/april2003/lacey. htm (Phase V, mostly). Their forensic scientists have had extensive training on subject. You, on, have most likely not the tools nor training to check a video for tampering., I'm not a CCTV expert, but, if police suspected tampering in CCTV footage, they could try to find evidences on control room computers, which requires complete physical access to control room. This something you cannot do, in any case: keeping "skills and tools" issue aside, no way a hotel could give you complete access to their security control room. 3) Is there any history records in system through it can be checked? It depends on system used by hotel. I you could try to see CCTV footage, perhaps to get hold of a copy, but in end you should definitely report the theft to police. They have authority, and possibly skills, to do some of things I mentioned above.

AVCHD is not an editing codec but an acquisition codec, means in to to edit footage, it need to be converted/transcoded into more suitable format. bottleneck is most AVCHD camcorders, record interlaced video, not suitable for computer/web use but only for televisions. means if you plan to use resulting video in computer screens,'ll need to de-interlace video (preferably prior importing to editing software, but after initial transcode). Canon released some camcorders record in 1080p (progressive - no need for de-interlacing) format, but don't think lot of models support this function yet. various workflows for these tasks, depend upon available software. My personal workflow from 1080i60 Sony videos (already copied to hdd) to Final Cut is: Rewrap AVCHD videos to Quicktime compatible format using ClipWrap ($49). This process is fast, because won't alter video files, just replace their container/headers. De-interlace videos and transcode them to editing codec (Apple Pro Res) using Jes Deinterlacer (free) Import them to FinalCut For will other ways also to reach to same result, but in to help you more, please let us know of what software you planning to use for editing your videos (I suppose iMovie be best choice).

Sony codes their recording in own format, hence. mt2s, they want you to use a Sony Laptop to edit footage., a Mac app called, MPEG Stream Clip, converts footage to any format you want at any frames/second you want. can download it for free from Squared 5, http://www. squared5. com/svideo/mpeg-streamclip-mac. html. It great piece of free software. for video editing software can use Apple's iMoive (for amateur) or purchase Apple's Final Cut Pro (wait until July, releasing new version).

MPEG-2 subject to license restrictions royalty payments, won't find much in of free software to edit MPEG-2 videos. can do this editing in QuickTime player with QuickTime Pro, but be aware MPEG-2 for DVDs uses complicated compression scheme using key frames and "difference" frames that repeat in regular pattern (Group of Pictures a. k. a GOP). cannot just edit out one frame without re-encoding rest if want to play it in DVD player.

Introduction problem lies with fact WhatsApp does not store history of your chats on its servers (except undelivered ones). means unlike other messaging providers, WhatsApp cannot repopulate your chat history on every device because no central location (server) stores them for you. this is a great step towards privatizing your chats, this makes things more difficult for your case. Analysis In early 2017, WhatsApp encrypted its backups to iCloud, means if you lost your iPhone prior to this, you may (optimistically) be able to read them in plain text. This would probably require to connect iPhone via cable to a third-party app on Mac/PC like iPhone Explorer or iExplorer. I used these years ago to extract files hidden in file system of old iPhone 4. But to absolutely no guarantee you will be able to open any WhatsApp files find (due to encryption). It seems to be entirely possible, to restore your current iPhone from backup of old one and view your messages that way. For worth, better off not risking your current chat threads, do a backup of your current state. you can always restore it to today's version if things start to go wrong. You may be interested in this article discusses ways to transfer chat histories to other phones (Android, in case you switched to one - didn't mention). Conclusion Based on (limited) options available to, I recommend trying the second one first greatest chance of reading messages, compared to option one and three. Please read through this guide to learn how to restore your chat history. interested if it works for you. Let me know how you get on.

ARP is layer 2. reason a broadcast is sent on layer 2 (data link layer) ARP normally not traverse to layer 3 (network layer). However it can provide extra features to layer 3 protocol. truth not all protocols fit OSI model exactly, because after it's just a model. If to push into spot say ARP is a layer 2. 5 protocol. It fits layer 2, but doesn't fit layer 3 completely. same discussion often held about ICMP and where it fits in: layer 3 or layer 4. good explanation on exceptions is: Normally, a protocol from layer N+1 is encapsulated with header of protocol from Layer N, but protocols like arp, stp, cdp, icmp and igmp are exceptions because encapsulated with a header of protocol from same layer.

IETF protocol suite not defined in term OSI model, hence mapping between IETF and OSI protocol is more a convention then. -in- good reasons to consider it a Layer 2 (it defined as an ethertype inside Ethernet-V2 frame, not forwarded by standard IP routers) as a layer 3 (it has to inter-operate with layer 3-to-2 mapping process of an host: a pure layer2 node not have), literature considering it a layer2 protocol is wider, commonly accepted as "layer 2" instead of "layer 3". But don't make it a dogma: speaking in term of layer 3 is not completely heretic: same process held into IPV6 (without ARP) is often defined as "layer 3" but it is exact conceptual process.

protocol number used by layer-3 protocol (IPv4 or IPv6) to determine to which layer-4 protocol in network stack should send payload of packet. port number is address for some layer-4 protocols (TCP or UDP). port number used by layer-4 protocol to determine which application gets payload of layer-4 datagram. routing protocol use protocol number in TCP header. believe you confusing layer-3 and layer-4. TCP header (layer 4) doesn't have field for protocol number - protocol number is in IP header (layer 3). Layers 2 to 4 each encapsulate datagram of layer above inside headers for layer. See this question and answer for more detail

Two separate VLANs must communicate through a layer-3 device, like a router. Devices on a VLAN communicate with each other using layer-2. Layer-3 used to communicate between separate layer-2 domains. Assuming most common communications (layer-2 is ethernet and layer-3 is IP), when a host on a VLAN wants to communicate with another host on same VLAN, it discovers other hosts layer-2 (e. MAC) address with like ARP, sends frame to MAC address. When a host on one VLAN wants to send something to host on another VLAN, it must use a layer-3 (e. IP) address. host use layer-2 to send frames to its defined gateway (router). router will strip off layer-2 frame inspect layer-3 packet for destination layer-3 address. router will then look up next hop for layer-3 address. create a new layer-2 frame for layer-3 packet based on layer-2 LAN on interface where it needs to send packet for next hop. Other routers in path to end LAN repeat this process until frame is placed on final VLAN, where receiving host gets the frame. You search for the OSI model and learn how it works. remember it is a model, some things in real world don't necessarily work exactly like model predict, but it will give gross understanding of how data travel from application on one host to application on another host.
Routing - Packets forwarded by layer 3 gateway, router. Switching - Frames forwarded by layer 2 switch. Forwarding - Protocol Data Units forwarded by networked / networking device.

Here's a way to transfer photos to your computer (Windows 8 and above) Connect your iPhone to trusted computer using lightning cable. important computer is trusted. iPhones do not connect to computer otherwise. Photos app should automatically open. If it does not, can open it using Windows start menu or search bar. Click on import button in top right corner, represented by downwards arrow in square box. Select photos you like to import. Follow prompts on screen. If'd like to delete imported photos, can click on check box in prompt. You will have your photos imported on your PC. Windows Vista and XP currently not supported for Photos.

To stage a file is to prepare it for commit. git exposes this action to users control allows to create partial commits, or to modify a file, stage it, modify it again, and only commit or revert to original modification. Staging allows finer control over how to approach version control.

To stage a file is to prepare it for a commit. Git, with its index allows to commit only certain parts of changes've done since last commit. Say you're working on two features - one finished, and one still needs work done. You'd like to make a commit and go home (5 o'clock, finally!) but wouldn't like to commit parts of second feature, not done yet. stage parts belong to first feature, and commit. Now your commit is your project with first feature done, while second is still in work-in-progress in your working directory.

Staging is a step before commit process in git., commit in git is performed in two steps: staging and actual commit. long as a changeset is in staging area, git allows you to edit it as like (replace staged files with other versions staged files, remove changes from staging, etc. ). Broken metaphor time: Consider a scenario where you call movers to get your stuff from old appartment to new appartment. Before, you go through your stuff, decide what you take with and what you throw away, pack it in bags leave it in main hallway. movers come, get packed) bags from hallway and transport them. In this example, everything until movers get your stuff, is staging: you decide what goes where, how to pack it (e. may decide half your stuff will be thrown away before movers get there - part of staging). From technical point of view, staging supports transactional commits, by splitting all operations into what can fail (staging) and what cannot fail (commit): commit in git is implemented transactionally, after staging is sucessfull. Several steps in staging can fail (for example, need to commit, but HDD is 99. 9999% full, git has no space to perform commit). This will fail in staging (your repository not be corrupted by partial commit) staging process doesn't affect commit history (it doesn't corrupt repository in case of error).

In English, "to stage" can mean organize and participate in (a public event): UDF supporters staged demonstration in Sofia (from http://oxforddictionaries. com/definition/stage ) name "staging" for git feature derives from this meaning: When staging, preparing and organizing a commit. a commit not quite the same as a performance, but important event in a VCS :-).

With most other version control systems, 2 places to store data: your working copy (the folders/files currently using) and datastore (where version control decides how to pack and store your changes). In Git third option: staging area (or index). basically a loading dock to determine what changes get shipped away. source: http://gitready. com/beginner/2009/01/18/the-staging-area. html

"stage" is a technically required intermediate step in process of checking in a file, collecting changes to be added to repository. Git's authors chose to make this step visible and persistent where other VCS make it a transient part of commit process. it's just an option that git gives you because it can why not?, main thing git "stage" gives you that other VCS don't is you can use it to checkpoint a file. It's effectively an unnamed, uncommented local commit gives intermediate step between done with all work and committing it to repository permanently and having nothing saved in local repo at. For example, let's say you have a feature partially finished. It's in stable state, passes tests, could go into production, but you have more work to do on it. You could stage all changes and then continue to work on feature. Later,'ll option to just commit what you staged (and push commit to remote repository) or to add new changes to staging area and then commit all at once, or to undo just your new changes and revert your working directory to state it in when you staged changes. It's possible to skip the staging area altogether and just use -a option to git commit if you don't find staging area helpful concept. Lots of people skip staging and GUI tools usually allow for this,.

you're confusing what on internally on switch. How it keeps track of which ports in which VLAN up to manufacturer. important to remember 802. 1q frames different format than "standard" Ethernet (802. 3). Standard Ethernet frames do not have VLAN IDs. PC or other device transmits and receives Ethernet frames (802. 3). When switch transmits frames on trunk, uses 802. 1q framing, includes VLAN tag. If switch transmitting frames with tags, then that port is a trunk port. Most hosts do not understand 802. 1q frames, they ignore them. why you can have tagged and untagged frames on same port. But it's still a trunk port.

think you're getting confused about terminology. Typically ports are often referred to as open, closed, or not reachable. An open port is one not blocked by NAT or firewall, has service answering requests at. example if enabled Web Sharing on Mac, standard HTTP port (80) would be open. A closed port is one reachable, but has no service to "answer" it. In some cases firewalls or routers with NAT will close ports, but usually this is port can be reached, but has no service there. unreachable port (which often show up in port scans as "timed out") is one where firewall or NAT ignores any attempt to contact it, rather than sending response says "this port is here, but closed". In theory this is more secure, since doesn't confirm to attacker a computer at IP they're touching. In reality benefit may be less, but'm not qualified enough to make definitive judgement. This is status will show up with most consumer routers and firewalls. You may want to try different port scanner, as in my tests, one you linked doesn't distinguish between closed and ports timed out.

's not normal to have ports open unless configured otherwise. You can find names of programs listening at these ports using following command in Terminal (under /Applications/Utilities): lsof -i :3128 lsof -i :8080 first column of output would be program name.

often confused point for people new to Networking, in particular to people up Cisco track, due to Cisco's over emphasis on this point. It more just a terminology thing. explain. 802. 1q standard defines method of tagging traffic between two switches to distinguish which traffic belongs to which VLANs. In Cisco terms, this is what happens on a "trunk" port. other vendors refer to this as a "tagged" port. In context, it means same: adding identifier to frames to indicate what VLAN frame belongs to. Terminology aside, main thing to in is VLAN tag is necessary, because often traffic traversing two switches belongs to multiple VLANs, must be way to determine which 1's and 0's belong to which VLAN. But what happens if a trunk port, expecting to receive traffic includes VLAN tag, receives traffic with no tag? In predecessor to 802. 1q, known as ISL (cisco proprietary, but archaic, no one supports it anymore, not even Cisco), untagged traffic on trunk would simply be dropped. 802. 1q however, provided for a way to not only receive this traffic, but also associate it to a VLAN of your choosing. This method is known as setting a Native VLAN., configure your trunk port with Native VLAN, whatever traffic arrives on port without existing VLAN tag, gets associated to your Native VLAN. As with all configuration items, if do not explicitly configure, usually default behavior exists. In case of Cisco (and most vendors), Default Native VLAN is VLAN 1. to, if not set Native VLAN explicitly, any untagged traffic received on trunk port is automatically placed in VLAN 1. trunk port is "opposite" from an Access Port. access port sends and expects to receive traffic with no VLAN tag.this work, an access port only sends and expects to receive traffic belonging to one VLAN. access port is statically configured for a particular VLAN, any traffic received on that port is internally associated on Switch as belonging to a particular VLAN (despite not tagging traffic for that VLAN when it leaves switch port)., to add to confusing mix. Cisco books refer to "default VLAN". The Default VLAN is the VLAN all Access Ports are assigned to until explicitly placed in another VLAN. In of Cisco switches (and most other Vendors, Default VLAN is usually VLAN 1. Typically, this VLAN is only relevant on an Access port, a port that sends and expects to receive traffic without a VLAN tag (also referred to an 'untagged port' by other vendors)., to summarize: Native VLAN can change. can set it to anything you like. Access Port VLAN can change. can set it to anything you like. Default Native VLAN is always 1, can not be change, because its set that way by Cisco Default VLAN is always 1, can not be changed, because it set that way by Cisco forgot other questions, can it / should it be changed? This is largely an opinion question. to agree with this school of thought: All unused ports should be in a specific VLAN. All active ports should be explicitly set on to a particular VLAN. Your switch should prevent traffic from traversing uplink into rest of network if traffic belongs on VLAN1, or VLAN you using for unused ports. Everything else should be allowed up the uplink. many different theories behind this. differing requirements would prevent restricted switch policy (scale, resources, etc).For instance, if a switch going into part of a network only one VLAN not VLAN 1, is possible to make "default" / native VLAN on all ports a particular VLAN using one global command, or preferred method to make all ports access ports and set access VLAN to 10 on each? You can not change default Cisco configurations. can use "interface range" to put all ports in different VLAN in one go. don't need to change Native VLAN on uplink trunk, so long as other switch is using same Native VLAN. If want to spare the switch from adding VLAN Tag, you could get creative do following (although, probably not recommended). Leave all access ports in the VLAN1. Leave Native VLAN at its default (VLAN1). On uplink switch, set the port as a trunk port. set its Native VLAN to the VLAN you want lower switch to be a part of. Since lower switch will send traffic to upper switch untagged, upper switch will receive it and associate it with it considers Native VLAN.

Yes it is. I use it for my firewall needs. great way to test if it still exists, is to run it. As for pf (the actual implementation of OS X is pfctl), it is more object orientated program control network access translation and packet filter (while ipfw requires external components). It born from OpenBSD (as opposed to FreeBSD) has been around for quite a while. It's power comes from to accomplish more internally, optimize long rulesets (that sometimes bogs ipfw down). They are both, excellent firewalls can coexist happily. read more about differences between pf and ipfw, here.

A closed port is one reachable, but has no service to "answer" it. In some cases firewalls or routers with NAT will close ports, but usually this is port can be reached, but has no service there. unreachable port (which often show up in port scans as "timed out") is one where firewall or NAT ignores any attempt to contact it, rather than sending response says "this port is here, but closed". In theory this is more secure, since doesn't confirm to attacker a computer at IP they're touching. In reality benefit may be less, but'm not qualified enough to make definitive judgement. This is status will show up with most consumer routers and firewalls. You may want to try different port scanner, as in my tests, one you linked doesn't distinguish between closed and ports timed out.

Physical cores are number of, actual hardware components. Logical cores are number of physical cores times number of threads run on each core through hyperthreading. for example, my 4-core processor runs two threads per core, so I have 8 logical processors.

Hyperthreading technology allows single physical processor core to behave like two logical processors. single processor core can execute two independent threads simultaneously. Intel refers to physical processor as a socket. Hyperthreading makes Physical Processor to behave like two Physical Processors, called Logical Processor. why? hyperthreading not double performance system, it can increase performance by better utilizing idle resources leading to greater throughput for certain important workload types. application running on one logical processor of busy core can expect slightly more than half of throughput it obtains while running alone on non-hyperthreaded processor. Physical cores are, physical cores within CPU. Logical cores are abilities of a single core to do 2 or more things simultaneously. grew out of early Pentium 4 CPUs ability to Hyper Threading (HTT). It was a a game played where sub components of core weren't used for certain instructions while, another long running instruction might have executed. CPU could work on 2 things simultaneously. Newer cores are more full-fledged CPUs're working on multiple things simultaneously, but aren't true CPUs as physical cores are. read more about limitations of hyperthreading functionality vs. physical capabilities of core on tomshardware in article titled: Intel Core i5 And Core i7: Intel’s Mainstream Magnum Opus. see breakdown of box using lscpu command: $ lscpu Architecture: x86_64 CPU op-mode(s): 32-bit, 64-bit CPU(s): 4 Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 2 CPU socket(s): 1 NUMA node(s): 1 Vendor ID: GenuineIntel CPU family: 6 Model: 37 Stepping: 5 CPU MHz: 2667. 000 Virtualization: VT-x L1d cache: 32K L1i cache: 32K L2 cache: 256K L3 cache: 3072K NUMA node0 CPU(s): 0-3 In my Intel i5 laptop has 4 "CPUs" in total CPU(s): 4 2 physical cores (1 socket × 2 cores/socket = 2 cores) Core(s) per socket: 2 CPU socket(s): 1 each can run up to 2 threads Thread(s) per core: 2 at the same time. These threads are core's logical capabilities.

Your computer has 2 cores, but 4 logical processors. seeing is Intel's hyper-threading technology. This technology puts multiple logical processors on single core, so each core can run multiple threads at once. difference between this and multiple cores is hyper-threading only duplicates parts of processor control current state, not actual execution unit, but multiple cores duplicate everything. This means computer will run like it has four cores only if threads on each core using different parts of execution unit, but if exact same thing was running on both threads in single core, it wouldn't be faster than two-core system without hyper-threading.

As an OS designer I agree with result of measurements. amount bullshit produced elsewhere about subject matter is unbelievable. See number of logical cores as number parallel threads/processes can be executed by HW. achieved by duplicating e. g. registers and instruction pointers of CPU core. CPU core itself decides which thread (instruction pointer) to use. It will decide to use other thread as instruction of current thread not available in cache and need to be fetched from e. g. memory or L3 cache. This mechanism create 10%-30% potential improvement in instructions/seconds or CPU performance. If run single application with one thread, you not able to reap this benefit, but if run two high load applications on e. g. old HT Pentium, you will be able to reap benefits. same true of for applications, have more then one thread. My Linux system has 200 threads, some benefits dependent on actual load are always present. All remarks apply without virtualization. Virtualbox only limits number of threads can run in parallel for each virtual machine (VM), but host process scheduler will change logical processor(s) and physical processor(s), on which VM processes run dynamically. If run high load applications on VM, additional logical cores will give you same benefit of 10%-30%. load can be single multi-threaded application or set of different applications. On modern systems with VT-x or AMD-V no performance penalty for maxing out number of logical cores, since also no noticeable performance penalty for running more virtual machines at same time. Your limit is performance of your CPU chip, so can't render videos on 3 VMs at same time without slowing down each VM, because they to share same physical CPU. Your host system might become irresponsive, if you render a video on a VM with all logical cores present, but have almost same problem, if you run that rendering app on your host.least in VM you have a choice could solve it by limiting max CPU load to 80%-90% or reducing number of cores for this reason.

IP address can broken down into two parts, Network Address and Host Address. In example, /29 refers to Subnet Mask 29 bits of total 32 bits from MSB to LSB are all 1's, i. e., 255. 255. 255. 248. This allow for 8 addresses per subnet. first address in subnet, 178. 18. 230. 120 is Network Address and - last address, is all 1's - i. e., 172. 18. 230. 127 is the Broadcast Address. host address can range anywhere between Network and Broadcast Address, i. e., 172. 18. 230. 121 to 172. 18. 230. 126. arrive at these addresses by performing logical AND on IP address and Subnet Mask. first IP address usually reserved for Network address and last one in block is for Broadcast address, remaining ones used as Host addresses. Loopback address is special reserved IP address, usually referred to as localhost - 127. 0. 0. 1 used to communicate with localhost. Host Addresses: Any other address between Network and Broadcast Addresses are Host Addressable, can be assigned to a Host and NOT reserved for any specific purpose, unlike Network and Broadcast Addresses.

DHCP and NAT have nothing in common (above "IP-related things"). elaborate what they do you find similar. DHCP assigns IP address, NAT mangles IP addresses (and higher level ports, like TCP/UDP), e. g. translates them to different address range.

DHCP for helping new clients network get IP address dynamically. (Without IP address, they're helpless. ) Dynamic NAT for translating clients already on network to different IP addresses dynamically. Using this, they appear to outside world like they have different address than they really do. only common thread between two is word "dynamic". When DHCP hands out addresses, it does so dynamically, means you might get different IP address next time. When NAT translates you, it does so dynamically, means might get translated to different port number or IP address next time.

Missing from current answers is DHCP is a protocol for configuring hosts, runs periodically to keep addresses and other configuration up to date. traffic is between host and DHCP server; typically both on same local network, but not always. NAT a process is for rewriting packets forwarded across a router. Specifically it translates addresses and sometimes ports. traffic is across router, typically between ISP and its client, or between two organisations.

, DHCP assigns IP addresses to hosts in private network, NAT converts private addresses into public addresses., NAT does not assign IP addresses to devices. It does, keep a table of IP address conversions, router uses to ensure packets between remote host and local host are not lost. NAT typically used to allow multiple devices on private network to share a single public IP address on a WAN interface. DHCP uses a pool of private addresses, such as 10. 0. 0. 0/8 pool, these addresses cannot be used on public network as internet., NAT must be used to convert private address, such as 10. 0. 0. 3, to public address, such as 209. 113. 65. 5, to allow host on private network to communicate with remote host.

article titled "AirPort Utility 6. x: Set NAT options for base station or AirPort Time Capsule" available at http://support. apple. com/kb/PH5103 has: To set NAT options, base station or AirPort Time Capsule must be set up to share Internet connection using DHCP and NAT. Open AirPort Utility, in Utilities folder in Applications folder. Select base station to set up, click Edit. Enter password if necessary. Click Network choose DHCP and NAT from Router Mode pop-up menu. Select Enable NAT Port Mapping Protocol. NAT Port Mapping Protocol (NAT-PMP) is Internet Engineering Task Force Internet Draft, alternative to common Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) protocol implemented in many NAT routers. NAT-PMP allows computer in private network (behind NAT router) to automatically configure router to allow clients outside private network to contact computer. Included in protocol is method for retrieving public IP address of NAT gateway, allows client to make public IP address and port number known to peers wish to communicate with it. protocol is implemented in current Apple products, including Mac OS X 10. 4 or later, AirPort Extreme and AirPort Express networking products, AirPort Time Capsule, and Bonjour for Windows. Select “Enable default host, ” enter IP address of host. default host is computer on network exposed to Internet and receives all inbound traffic. default host may be useful if use computer on AirPort network to play network games, or want to route all Internet traffic through single computer. can also set up port mapping to direct network traffic to specific computer on network. article titled "AirPort Utility software and firmware downloads" available at http://support. apple. com/kb/ht1998 tells you where to get Airport Utility.

AirPort base stations set up internal NAT gateway code for full /24 network (10. 0. 1. x by default). means IP addresses. 2 through. 254 are available for machines connected to network. But AirPort base stations configure internal DHCP servers by default to only serve out addresses. 2 through. 200 via DHCP. 201 through. 254 are already set aside for manually/statically configured hosts. manually configure your server machine to be on one of upper 54 addresses (. 201 through. 254) and it'll just work., even if manually configured host to use one addresses base station's DHCP server usually hands out, base station smart not to try to serve out that address to other client while your other machine using it. UI you see on later base stations is to make base station's built-in DHCP server give same host same IP address lease via DHCP each time, based on host's MAC address. convenient if you have a laptop you take to different networks all time, want to leave laptop configured for DHCP. But if have a machine to on your network all the time because it's server, you can just configure that server machine's IP address manually, on server. Letting other hosts on Internet get to your server is a separate issue. For that, you have to set up Default Host (some other products call this "DMZ") or Port Mapping (a. Port Forwarding).

VirtualBox DHCP is working properly. nothing wrong with having all of your machines getting same address in NAT configuration. All VMs are isolated from each other no risk of conflict. They not on the same adapter. Each VM has its own virtualized hardware including NICs. default gateway need not to be 10. 0. 2. 1. Although it common practice to have it at lower IP address, it can be any IP in subnet range., no "real" dhcp service, everything is hardcoded in VirtualBox code, although if not happy with default IP addresses you can fine tune the NAT engine.

DHCP server knows client Mac address from DHCP client discover message offer message contains. proposed IP address for client example 172. 16. 2. 16 subnet mask identify subnet space example 255. 255. 255. 0 IP of default gateway for subnet example 172. 16. 2. 1 Internal dns server ip address if hosted, other external dns address used as configured on DHCP pool. conclude DHCP offer message is unicast from DHCP server

From Apple Support Knowledge Base. Time Capsule, Mac OS X v10. 6. 3 or later: How to transfer your back up from existing Time Capsule to new one For process, leave computer in same room as Time Capsules, or use one Ethernet cable to connect Mac to Ethernet port on existing Time Capsule, then use another Ethernet cable to connect from existing Time Capsule to new Time Capsule. Configure your Time Capsule for network. See documentation with Time Capsule for information about setting it up on network. Open Time Machine preferences in System Preferences. Slide Time Machine switch to Off. Open Finder window. Locate both Time Capsules listed in SHARED section of navigation pane on left of Finder window. Note: If not see Time Capsules in section, choose Preferences from Finder menu and make sure "Connected servers" is checked under SHARED. Select name of new Time Capsule in navigation pane. default name is "Time Capsule xxxxxx", with xxxxxx being last digits of ID printed on bottom of Time Capsule. Mount volume by double-clicking name of volume in Finder window's main section. default drive name is "Data". Open new Finder window by pressing Command-N, or by choosing File > New Finder Window. Repeat previous 2 steps with other Time Capsule, to mount it. Drag backup disk image from current Time Capsule to new Time Capsule. This can take time to complete because entire backup will be copied. Open Time Machine preferences in System Preferences. Click "Select Disk. ", then select your new Time Capsule. Perform a Time Machine back up. After back up, remove Ethernet cables if desired and configure wireless network to your liking.

By default, Nmap scans most common 1, 000 ports for each protocol(tcp, udp). If your port outside it won't scan it hence won't report it. However, can specify ports want to scan with -p option.

'Filtered port' statement from nmap differs according scan method. standard scan (TCP Scan if unprivileged user, or Half-Open scan -sS if superuser) relies on TCP protocol. (named 3-way hanshake) client (you) issues a SYN, if server replies SYN/ACK : it means port is open ! You issue a SYN, if server replies RST : it means port is close ! You issue a SYN, if server not reply, or replies with ICMP error : it means port is filtered. Likely IDS / statefull firewall block request) To figure real status of port, can : use -sV, or -A option (version detection, help to determine status port. use --tcp-flags SYN, FIN to try bypassing fw. use other scan types (http://nmap. org/book/man-port-scanning-techniques. html) "Nmap Network Discovery" book, written by creator Fyodor explains this well. I quote filtered : Nmap cannot determine whether port is open because packet filtering prevents probes from reaching port. filtering could be from dedicated firewall device, router rules, or host-based firewall software. These ports frustrate attackers because provide little information. respond with ICMP error messages as type 3 code 13 (destination unreachable: communication administratively prohibited), but filters that drop probes without responding are more common. This forces Nmap to retry several times in case probe was dropped due to network congestion rather than filtering. This filtering slows scans down dramatically. open|filtered : Nmap places ports in this state when unable to determine whether port is open or filtered. This occurs for scan types in which open ports give no response. lack of response could also mean packet filter dropped probe or response elicited. Nmap does not know for sure whether port is open or filtered.UDP, IP protocol, FIN, NULL, and Xmas scans classify ports this way. closed|filtered : state used when Nmap unable to determine port closed or filtered. only used for IP ID Idle scan discussed in Section 5. 10, "TCP Idle Scan (-sl)

'Filtered port' statement from nmap differs according scan method. standard scan (TCP Scan if unprivileged user, or Half-Open scan -sS if superuser) relies on TCP protocol. (named 3-way hanshake) client (you) issues a SYN, if server replies SYN/ACK : it means port is open ! You issue a SYN, if server replies RST : it means port is close ! You issue a SYN, if server not reply, or replies with ICMP error : it means port is filtered. Likely IDS / statefull firewall block request) To figure real status of port, can : use -sV, or -A option (version detection, help to determine status port. use --tcp-flags SYN, FIN to try bypassing fw. use other scan types (http://nmap. org/book/man-port-scanning-techniques. html) "Nmap Network Discovery" book, written by creator Fyodor explains this well. I quote filtered : Nmap cannot determine whether port is open because packet filtering prevents probes from reaching port. filtering could be from dedicated firewall device, router rules, or host-based firewall software. These ports frustrate attackers because provide little information. respond with ICMP error messages as type 3 code 13 (destination unreachable: communication administratively prohibited), but filters that drop probes without responding are more common. This forces Nmap to retry several times in case probe was dropped due to network congestion rather than filtering. This filtering slows scans down dramatically. open|filtered : Nmap places ports in this state when unable to determine whether port is open or filtered. This occurs for scan types in which open ports give no response. lack of response could also mean packet filter dropped probe or response elicited. Nmap does not know for sure whether port is open or filtered.UDP, IP protocol, FIN, NULL, and Xmas scans classify ports this way. closed|filtered : state used when Nmap unable to determine port closed or filtered. only used for IP ID Idle scan discussed in Section 5. 10, "TCP Idle Scan (-sl)

You scanning empty space. -Pn option (formerly -PN or -P0) tells Nmap to skip host discovery step (colloquially called "ping scan") assume every target address has a host listening on it. For default TCP scan, means Nmap will scan 1000 different ports on every target address, regardless of replies received. When no reply received for a probe, Nmap will wait a full timeout period (default starts at 1 second) then retry a few times to ensure packet not dropped. Your valuable bandwidth (and time) is wasted sending probes never get response. important part host discovery plays is in giving Nmap baseline for how fast and responsive your network connection is. In doing "ping sweep, " Nmap discovers round-trip time for each target. It can more accurately determine when packet was dropped should be retried, or when sending too many packets at once. Without this information, Nmap has to play it safe, slowing down sending rate making extra retransmissions to make sure no packets are lost. In, -Pn option not usually useful, though one of most commonly used and recommended ones.

Yes. protocol no longer secure, cracking initial MS-CHAPv2 authentication can be reduced to difficulty of cracking a single DES 56-bit key, with current computers can be brute-forced in short time (making strong password irrelevant to security of PPTP as entire 56-bit keyspace can be searched within practical time constraints). attacker can do MITM to capture handshake (and any PPTP traffic after), do offline crack of handshake and derive RC4 key. Then, attacker will able to decrypt and analyse traffic carried in PPTP VPN. PPTP not provide forward secrecy, just cracking one PPTP session is sufficient to crack all previous PPTP sessions using same credentials., PPTP provides weak protection to integrity of data being tunneled. RC4 cipher, while providing encryption, does not verify integrity of data not an Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) cipher. PPTP doesn't do additional integrity checks on traffic (such as HMAC), vulnerable to bit-flipping attacks,. attacker can modify PPTP packets with little possibility of detection. Various discovered attacks on RC4 cipher (such as Royal Holloway attack) make RC4 a bad choice for securing large amounts of transmitted data, VPNs are prime candidate for such attacks as they by nature usually transmit sensitive and large amounts of data. Building on @Josh's answer, some legacy services require use of a hashing algorithm called MS/CHAP. of unfortunate properties of MS/CHAP hash family is stored hash is weak enough to allow password to be retrieved. This is a problem if file in server containing hashes gets stolen by attacker. The PPTP VPN server is one of legacy services use MS/CHAP. said, you do not need to weaken hash of server administrator if person not using VPN. Users created after Server. app is installed and set up will have their hashes weakened. You can use pwpolicy(8) tool to see what hashes are saved for a user. If user created before VPN was started and you wish to have them use service, you can go to users pane and look up that user, you will see a message "the user may not be able to access all services" with option to fix. Choose fix. it always a good idea to have a specific user for server administration tasks. I encourage you to create a user for running Server. app and subsequently no need to weaken hashes for that user.

first answer is nobody knows why languages become popular, anybody who says otherwise is deluded or has agenda. (It's often easy to identify why a language fails to become popular, but's another question. ) With disclaimer, here some points suggestive, most important first: first mature C compiler appeared in 1974; first mature OCaml compiler appeared in late 1990s. C has 25-year head start. C shipped with Unix, was biggest "killer app" of all time. For long time, every CS department had to have Unix, meant every instructor and everyone taking CS course had opportunity to be exposed to C. OCaml and ML still waiting for their first killer app. (MLdonkey is cool, but it's not Unix. ) C fills its niche well I doubt there will never be another low-level language devoted only to systems programming. (To evidence in favor, read Dennis Ritchie's paper on history of C from HOPL II. ) not clear what OCaml's niche is, and Standard ML's niche is only a little clearer. Caml and ML have few competitors, C killed off its only competitor (BLISS). C's great strengths is its cost model is very predictable: easy to look at any small fragment of C code get accurate idea of machine operations to performed to execute code. OCaml's cost model less clear, especially because memory allocation is less explicit, overall cost of memory allocation cost allocation plus costs during garbage collection) depends on emergent properties like how long objects live and which objects refer to other objects. net result is performance is hard to predict, hard to analyze after the fact. (OCaml's memory-profiling tools are not what they should be. ) As result, OCaml is not good for applications where performance must be very predictable---like embedded systems.C is a language with a standard many compilers. OCaml is a software artifact: only compiler is from a single source, and compiler is the standard. standard changes with every release. For people who value stability and backward compatibility, single-source language may represent unacceptable risk. Anybody with a halfway-decent undergraduate compiler course and of persistence can write a C compiler that more or less works, with adequate performance. To get implementation of OCaml or ML off ground requires more education, to get comparable performance to naive C compiler requires more work. This means fewer hobbyists to mess around with languages like OCaml, it's harder tor community to develop deep understanding about how to exploit it.

like hostnames and domain names, username not strictly a Unix thing but can often span wider range of OS types. they considered case sensitive depends on standard used to specify them. Hostnames and domain names are clearly case insensitive by DNS standard (see RFC4343). Usernames stored on local backend (/etc/passwd) or Unix style one (NIS) not case insensitive by POSIX standard. Usernames stored in LDAP or Active Directory backend will follow used attribute schema definition, uid and cn often storing user name have differing schema attributes, case insensitive for former but case sensitive for latter. means both Abc and abc might match or not abc's entry depending on ldap server configuration. Due to this inconsistency, recommend to only use lowercase for both usernames and host/domain name and avoid ssh ABC@SERVERNAME. DOMAIN. COM which is rude anyway.

Unix usernames are definitely case-sensitive, more, using usernames with uppercase characters on Unix systems can produce unwanted results, should generally be avoided. examples are: It can break email for user. standards for SMTP allow email addresses to be case-insensitive, by default MTA receiving message will fold email address to lowercase to find user to deliver to. If username has uppercase characters it not be resolved without special config overrides to cater for this. (this affects MTAs as sendmail, postfix etc and delivery processing agents like procmail) Many early hardware terminals were not case sensitive. common they only used uppercase. When logging in to some versions of Unix, starting a login name with an uppercase character will trigger system to assume you're using ancient uppercase only terminal will enable case folding - converts all of entered uppercase to lowercase (you to escape uppercase characters to say they're uppercase) to help you to enter username it expects be in lowercase. I don't believe this is a thing on Linux, but've seen it demonstrated on HP-UX. As long been convention to only use lowercase characters in usernames, reasonable to expect other tools (some may not thought of) on system may also assume username should be lowercase, and make checks, conversions etc accordingly, thus breaking things for user.

user names are definitely case sensitive. test this by adding two users with similar names: ~ # useradd foobar ~ # useradd fooBar ~ # grep ^foo /etc/passwd foobar:x:1001:1001::/home/foobar:/bin/sh fooBar:x:1002:1002::/home/fooBar:/bin/sh This question/answer shows how to compensate for someone trying to log in with username "wrong" case according to LDAP servers. note this will only work if usernames all listed as lowercase (or can make all uppercase if want).

Note uppercase and lowercase letters allowed in domain names, no significance attached to case. referenced RFC 1034 echos this: Note while upper and lower case letters allowed in domain names, no significance attached to case., two names with same spelling but different case to be treated as if identical. ssh tool stores known remote computer IP address and remote ssh key identification in ~/. ssh directory. can read up on this by consulting manual page on mac man ssh or on internet. may need to read entire article and do follow up research if first exposure with ssh - but relevant section for warning you pasted goes thusly: ssh automatically maintains and checks database containing identification for all hosts it been used with. Host keys stored in ~/. ssh/known_hosts in user's home directory. Addition- ally, file /etc/ssh_known_hosts is automatically checked for known hosts. new hosts are auto- matically added to user's file. You can turn off storing, warning or clear cache if don't care to investigate more. This a useful tool for people that ssh into fixed servers and need to know when things like above change.

correct file, prior to Mavericks, was ~/. MacOSX/environment. plist. This no longer supported. In Darwin, and therefore in Mac OS X, proper place to set these is in /etc/launchd. conf to apply to all processes; if relating to user shells specifically, use appropriate shell files instead, depending on shell in question. See launchd. conf and launchctl man pages for more. If goal is to see these applied for ssh sessions need to be aware ssh, for security reasons, doesn't apply environment variables in this manner. In ssh session normally receives more restrictive set of environment variables from OS as it's not known as a "login" or "interactive" shell, classified as an "non-interactive" shell. (See man bash for more on shell types. ) ssh handles environment variables well covered in ssh/sshd docs and man pages. For ssh -- is it's own shell, akin to bash -- environment variables for session are stored in ~/. ssh/environment as per-user equivalent of setting these for bash or csh, etc in relevant launch files. This is probably where you want to set your ENV variables for user ssh sessions, don't detail why looking to assign ENVs globally in original post, helpful in solution. suggest set them explicitly on user per user basis to maintain proper security based on each respective account following least restrictive privilege/attribute best practice. If for wish to ignore security implications of this, set PermitUserEnvironment in ssh configs. Note this is disabled if UseLogin is enabled. IMPORTANT: Realize this means user accounts set to use /bin/false as their shell - typical method for disabling user account - can now potentially get around this restriction and could become active, is dangerous.Many accounts set to use /bin/false as shell security expectation. you shouldn't be doing this globally expecting ssh to propagate ENV for security reasons. Your question is, effectively, purposely asking how to defeat several mechanisms exist for security reasons.

"stage" is a technically required intermediate step in process of checking in a file, collecting changes to be added to repository. Git's authors chose to make this step visible and persistent where other VCS make it a transient part of commit process. it's just an option that git gives you because it can why not?, main thing git "stage" gives you that other VCS don't is you can use it to checkpoint a file. It's effectively an unnamed, uncommented local commit gives intermediate step between done with all work and committing it to repository permanently and having nothing saved in local repo at. For example, let's say you have a feature partially finished. It's in stable state, passes tests, could go into production, but you have more work to do on it. You could stage all changes and then continue to work on feature. Later,'ll option to just commit what you staged (and push commit to remote repository) or to add new changes to staging area and then commit all at once, or to undo just your new changes and revert your working directory to state it in when you staged changes. It's possible to skip the staging area altogether and just use -a option to git commit if you don't find staging area helpful concept. Lots of people skip staging and GUI tools usually allow for this,.

To stage a file is to prepare it for commit. git exposes this action to users control allows to create partial commits, or to modify a file, stage it, modify it again, and only commit or revert to original modification. Staging allows finer control over how to approach version control.
