First, important things: Bash isn't going away. If you already using bash, nothing change for. All changes is zsh will be default login shell for new accounts, you can select bash instead. Scripts not affected. What changes is shell for interactive use,. shell in terminals (and few other things use login shell, such as crontabs). If a script in file with execution permissions, starting with shebang line such as #!/bin/bash or #!/bin/sh or #!/usr/bin/env bash, it'll keep working as before. Zsh's syntax not completely compatible with bash, but it's close. lot of code will keep working, for example typical aliases and functions. main differences are in interactive configuration features., assuming considering switching to zsh, possibility for years, here main differences you'll encounter. not exhaustive list! Main differences for interactive use Configuration files: bash reads (mainly). bashrc in non-login interactive shells (but macOS starts login shell in terminals by default),. profile or. bash_profile in login shells, and. inputrc. Zsh reads (mainly). zshrc (in all interactive shells) and. zprofile (in login shells). This means none of bash customizations will apply: need to port them over. can't just copy files many things need tweaking. Key bindings use different syntax. Bash uses. inputrc and bind builtin to bind keys to readline commands. Zsh uses bindkey builtin to bind keys to zle widgets. Most readline commands have zsh equivalent, but isn't always a perfect equivalence.Speaking key bindings, if use Vi(m) as in-terminal editor not as command line mode in shell, notice zsh defaults to vi editing mode if EDITOR or VISUAL set to vi or vim. bindkey -e switches to emacs mode. Prompt: bash sets prompt (mainly) from PS1 contains backslash escapes. Zsh sets prompt mainly from PS1 contains percent escapes. functionality of bash's PROMPT_COMMAND available in zsh via precmd and preexec hook functions. Zsh has more convenience mechanisms to build fancy prompts including prompt theme mechanism. basic command line history mechanisms (navigation with Up/Down, search with Ctrl+R, history expansion with !! and friends, last argument recall with Alt+. or $_) work in same way, but lot of differences in details, too many to list here. can copy your. bash_history to. zsh_history if haven't changed shell option changes file format. Completion: both shells default to basic completion mode mostly completes command and file names, switch to fancy mode by including bash_completion on bash or by running compinit in zsh. some commands bash handles better and some zsh handles better. Zsh is usually more precise, but sometimes gives up where bash does isn't correct but sensible. To specify possible completions for command, zsh has three mechanisms: “old” completion mechanism with compctl forget about. “new” completion mechanism with compadd and lots functions begin with underscore and powerful complex user configuration mechanism. emulation to support bash completion functions enable by running bashcompinit. emulation isn't 100% perfect but usually works. Many bash's shopt settings have corresponding setopt in zsh.Zsh doesn't treat # as comment start on command line by default, only in scripts (including. zshrc. To enable interactive comments, run setopt interactive_comments. differences for scripting (and power users on command line) In bash, $foo takes value of foo, splits it at whitespace characters, for each whitespace-separated part, if contains wildcard characters and matches existing file, replaces pattern by list of matches. To get value of foo, need "$foo". same applies to command substitution $(foo). In zsh, $foo is value of foo and $(foo) is output of foo minus final newlines, with two exceptions. If word becomes empty due to expanding empty unquoted variables, it's removed. a=; b=; printf "%s\n" one "$a$b" three $a$b five prints one, empty line, three, five). result of unquoted command substitution is split at whitespace pieces don't undergo wildcard matching. Bash arrays are indexed from 0 to (length-1). Zsh arrays indexed from 1 to length. With a=(one two three), in bash, ${a[1]} is two, in zsh, it's one. In bash, if reference array variable without braces, get first element,. $a is one and $a[1] is one[1]. In zsh, $a expands to list of non-empty elements, $a[1] expands to first element., in bash, length of array is ${#a}; also works in zsh but can write it more simply as $#a. can make 0-indexing default with setopt ksh_arrays turns on requirement to use braces to refer to array element.Bash has extra wildcard patterns as @(foo|bar) to match foo or bar, only enabled with shopt -s extglob. In zsh, can enable these patterns with setopt ksh_glob, but also simpler-to-type native syntax such as (foo|bar), requires setopt extended_glob (do put that in your. zshrc, it's on by default in completion functions). **/ for recursive directory traversal is always enabled in zsh. In bash, by default, if wildcard pattern doesn't match file, it's left unchanged. In zsh, by default, you'll get an error, usually safest setting. If want to pass wildcard parameter to command, use quotes. can switch to bash behavior with setopt no_nomatch. make non-matching wildcard patterns expand to empty list instead with setopt null_glob. In bash, right-hand side of pipeline runs in a subshell. In zsh, it runs in parent shell, can write things like somecommand | read output. Some nice zsh features a few nice zsh features bash doesn't have (at not without serious elbow grease)., selection of ones most useful. Glob qualifiers allow matching files based on metadata time stamp, size, etc. allow tweaking output. syntax is rather cryptic, but extremely convenient. few examples: foo*(. ): only regular files matching foo* and symbolic links to regular files, not directories and other special files. foo*(*. ): only executable regular files matching foo*. foo*(-. ): only regular files matching foo*, not symbolic links and other special files. foo*(-@): only dangling symbolic links matching foo*. foo*(om): files matching foo*, sorted by last modification date, most recent first.pass this to ls, it'll do its own sorting. useful in... foo*(om[1, 10]): 10 most recent files matching foo*, recent first. foo*(Lm+1): files matching foo* size at least 1MB. foo*(N): same as foo*, but if doesn't match file, produce empty list regardless of setting null_glob option (see above). *(D): match all files including dot files (except. and. ). foo/bar/*(:t) (using history modifier): files in foo/bar, with only base name of file. E. g. if foo/bar/qux. txt, expanded as qux. txt. foo/bar/*(. :r): take regular files under foo/bar remove extension. E. g. foo/bar/qux. txt expanded as foo/bar/qux. foo*. odt(e\''REPLY=$REPLY:r. pdf'\'): take list of files matching foo*. odt, replace. odt by. pdf (regardless of PDF file exists). few useful zsh-specific wildcard patterns. foo*. txt~foobar*: all. txt files whose name starts with foo but not foobar. image<->. jpg(n): all. jpg files whose base name is image followed by number, e. g. image3. jpg and image22. jpg but not image-backup. jpg. glob qualifier (n) causes files to be listed in numerical order,. image9. jpg comes before image10. jpg (you make this default even without -n with setopt numeric_glob_sort). To mass-rename files, zsh provides convenient tool: zmv function. Suggested for.zshrc: autoload zmv alias zcp='zmv -C' zln='zmv -L' Example: zmv '(*). jpeg' '$1. jpg' zmv '(*)-backup. (*)' 'backups/$1. $2' Bash has few ways to apply transformations when taking value of a variable. Zsh has some of same and many more. Zsh has little convenient features to change directories. Turn on setopt auto_cd to change to a directory when type its name without having to type cd (bash also has this nowadays). use two-argument form to cd to change to directory name close to current directory. For example, if in /some/where/foo-old/deeply/nested/inside want to go to /some/where/foo-new/deeply/nested/inside, just type cd old new. To assign value to variable, write VARIABLE=VALUE. To edit value of variable interactively, run vared VARIABLE. Final advice Zsh comes with configuration interface supports common settings, including canned recipes for like case-insensitive completion. To (re)run this interface (the first line not needed if using a configuration file edited by zsh-newuser-install): autoload -U zsh-newuser-install zsh-newuser-install Out of box, with no configuration file, many of zsh's useful features disabled for backward compatibility with 1990's versions. zsh-newuser-install suggests recommended features to turn on. many zsh configuration frameworks on web (many on Github). They can be convenient way to get started with powerful features. flip side of coin is they often lock you in doing things the way author does, sometimes they'll prevent you from doing things the way you want. Use them at your own risk.zsh manual has lot of information, but's often written in way terse hard to follow, has few examples. Don't hesitate to search for explanations and examples online: if only use part of zsh's easy to understand in manual, you'll miss out. Two good resources are zsh-users mailing list and Unix Stack Exchange. extensive collection of articles on switching to zsh on mac can found on scriptingosx. com and useful Ruby script to bring command history with you, can found on Github.

For those looking for command completion solution for bash as easy to use as zsh + oh-my-zsh, now bash-it project., in its own words, is "a shameless ripoff of oh-my-zsh" -- nothing wrong with! It sets up plugin like architecture like oh-my-zsh does, bring things in and out of environment easily get new things via sync'ing to their github project. Installation needs three steps: Check clone of this repo: git clone https://github. com/revans/bash-it. git ~/. bash_it Run ~/. bash_it/install. sh (it automatically backs up your ~/. bash_profile) Edit ~/. bash_profile file to customize bash-it. If afraid of full-on switch to zsh, bash-it is nice middle ground keeps you on bash but gives powerful plugins to extend environment with.

Not a bash answer, as I don't have one, but if you switch your shell to zsh (a close relative of bash) install configuration framework prezto you'll get this functionality more or less out of the box, significantly better autocompletion. Switching to zsh likely won't change day to day bash workflow all, but it'll open of doors in of customisation and extension, adds clever features worth learning - like shared command history across all prompts included in autocompletion dictionary, file globbing to efficiently work with multiple files at once, importantly compatibility modes, whereby zsh can emulate another shell - meaning if some bash scripts don't work to after switching to zsh, you can just emulate it - although personally all bash scripts I've written still worked fine in zsh. Useful links: Installing latest version of zsh in OS X Installing prezto in-depth discussion of how switching can improve workflow

1. Is way to see what key combination already taken, and for what purpose? can see if conflict with your chosen shortcut. From "If keyboard shortcut doesn’t work": Choose Apple menu > System Preferences, then click Keyboard. Click Keyboard Shortcuts. yellow warning triangle appears next to conflicting keyboard shortcuts. 2. key combination convention or rule for different modifier keys? What key appropriate for what task? (e. g. when I choose Command or Shift or Option or Ctrl or one of function keys) For dictionary lookups, Apple defined Ctrl+Cmd+D as "Display definition of selected word in Dictionary app. " OS X Human Interface Guidelines on Keyboard Shortcuts states following about when to use these modifier keys and for what purposes. recommended priority is to use Cmd frequently, use Option sparingly, avoid using Ctrl and use Shift for complementary functions of common command (of, may observe in certain instances Apple does not follow these guidelines). Quote from Keyboard Shortcuts page: possible, use Command key as main modifier key in keyboard shortcut. For example, Command-P uses Command to modify P key. For command that complements another more common command, can add Shift to shortcut. For example, shortcut for complementary Page Setup command adds Shift to shortcut for Print to give Shift-Command-P. Use Option key sparingly. If third, less common command related to pair of commands that use Command and Shift-Command, can use Option-Command for third command’s keyboard equivalent. Use combinations like these very rarely. can also use Option for a keyboard shortcut that’s convenience or power-user feature. For example, Finder uses Option-Command-W for Close All Windows and Option-Command-M for Minimize All Windows. possible, avoid using Control key.Control key used by universal access features—as in Cocoa text fields where Emacs-style key bindings often used—it should be used as a modifier key only when necessary. difference in return key determined by physical/mechanical standard used. Europe uses ISO standard with "skinny" return US (and Australia where I am) use ANSI standard. to OSPF RFC 2328 (10. 6): If Interface MTU field in Database Description packet indicates IP datagram size larger than router can accept on receiving interface without fragmentation, Database Description packet is rejected. simple answer is standard was designed to drop datagrams too large instead of fragmenting them. Fragmented traffic increases CPU burden of device and decreases performance of need for fragmentation needed extra traffic. goal of dynamic routing protocol is be stable and fast converging protocol, anything contrary to those goals should be eliminated. Setting requirement for MTUs to match helps enforce this performance requirement. More from OSPF RFC: 4. 3. Routing protocol packets OSPF protocol runs directly over IP, using IP protocol 89. OSPF does not provide explicit fragmentation/reassembly support. When fragmentation is necessary, IP fragmentation/reassembly is used. OSPF protocol packets designed so large protocol packets can be split into several smaller protocol packets. This practice is recommended; IP fragmentation should be avoided whenever possible.

Pete said: can't think of situation you need this. just wanted to know logic makes this explicit check in routing protocols. Short answer Routing protocols are fundamental building blocks on internet; we need them to be reliable in every possible case. does no good to bring up OSPF or EIGRP adjacency on mismatched MTU. Routing protocols must remove potential mismatched MTUs from router's forwarding path. Long answer can think of three possible situations find mismatched IGP MTUs. Unintentional MTU mismatch at Layer2 (for instance, if someone accidentally mismatched MTUs on serial line, or different vendors had different default MTUs on same media) Matching Layer2 MTUs, but router implementation has bug miscalculates required interface IP MTU Intentional MTU mismatch IP MTUs directly correlated to Layer2 MTUs (at least for Case 1, above). No matter what we do, we always at mercy of mitigating problems from unintentional Layer2 MTU mismatches, no Layer2 MTU discovery mechanism (unlike IP, has ICMP error messages). This means have to do everything possible to avoid Layer2 MTU mismatches, even if Cases 2 and 3 above are casualties of mitigating problems with Case number 1. Case 1 has colossal implications unless we solve it;. black-holing all traffic just because permitted mismatched MTUs. always limited to least common denominator on link. Frames larger than receive MTU of interface are silently discarded, router has no way of knowing whether MTU was intentionally mismatched, or happened accidentally., EIGRP and OSPF require valid Layer2 adjacencies Note 1 (including MTUs).What(Could) consequence without matching MTU? Quoting John Moy (OSPF's author) in RFC 2329 Page 4: Problems with all IP forwarding OSPF Problems quoting him from OSPF mailing list: Note 1 some people misunderstand meaning of adjacency as strictly IP routing protocol concept. assertion misses reality everything (including IP) requires matching layer2 MTUs, for Layer2 domains to work properly. important functions of routing protocol is building valid FIB / CEF / forwarding table. table maps information learned via routing protocols to layer2 rewrite info. Layer2 relationships on same physical link are Cisco also calls adjacencies.

From "OSPF: Anatomy of a Routing Protocol" by John Moy, who wrote much of OSPF specification. exchange of routing information between areas is essentially Distance Vector. With Distance Vector, larger number of redundant paths worse your convergence properties get. OSPF requires all areas to attach directly to backbone limits topology to simple hub and spoke topology. This eliminates redundant paths and prevents from 'count to infinity' problems.

OSPF Backbone Why is area 0 backbone area in OSPF? Why must all other areas connect to it? explained in RFC 3509, Section 1. 21: 1. 2 Motivation In OSPF domains area topology restricted must be a backbone area (area 0) all other areas must have physical or virtual connections to backbone. reason for star-like topology is OSPF inter-area routing uses distance-vector approach strict area hierarchy permits avoidance "counting to infinity" problem. OSPF prevents inter-area routing loops by implementing split-horizon mechanism, allowing ABRs to inject into backbone only Summary-LSAs from intra-area routes, limiting ABRs' SPF calculation to consider only Summary-LSAs in backbone area's link-state database. OSPF usually considered link-state protocol. OSPF uses both link-state protocol and distance-vector protocol algorithms. Routes within backbone, or non-backbone area computed as link-state protocol (ref Dijkstra's algorithm). When OSPF must carry non-backbone routes through backbone, uses distance-vector behavior (i. parts Bellman Ford algorithm) to propagate Type3 LSA metrics into non-backbone areas. example of OSPF's distance-vector behavior: <-- Area 5 --><- Area 0 --><- Area 4 --> R5-----------R1-----------R2------------R3---------------------R4 Cost 3 Cost 5 Cost 7 Cost 12 LSA--> LSA--> Type3 LSA Type3 LSA {From R1} {From R2} R5 cost is 3 R5 cost is 8 Consider what happens to /32 Loopback route for R5. R5 sends Type1 LSA containing /32 Loopback R1 (Area 5 ABR), connected to Area 0; it translates Type1 LSA into Type3 LSA with cost of 3.R2 (Area 4 ABR) receives R1's Type3 LSA (metric 3) changes metric to R5's Loopback, based on R2's cost to R1. Now R2's Type3 LSA for R5 has cost of 8. This is distance-vector behavior mentioned above. Requiring all non-backbone routes to go through backbone is a loop-prevention mechanism. Connecting non-backbone OSPF areas at ABR If 2 areas aren't connected through area 0 (discontiguous), OSPF as link state protocol increase possibility of routing loops?, OSPF uses distance-vector behavior to send routes through Area 0 backbone. Distance-vector protocols have limits, count-to-infinity problem. OSPF would be vulnerable to same issues, if didn't boundaries on behavior. 1RFC 3509 describes Cisco IOS's ABR behavior

You can read about finer workings of these protocols for yourself, they thoroughly documented on Internet it's a doddle to find information on them. From practicle perspective in case of EIGRP vs OSPF, OSPF always wins for following reasons: Convergence Speed: Everyone mentioned EIGRP faster than OSPF using default settings. If deploy either protocol without reading about them and use their default settings, you clearly don't know what you are doing in my opinion. Why deploy default settings without knowing what they are, when realise what they are realise OSPF supports BFD becomes lightening quick (as does ISIS). Traffic Engineering: OSPF like ISIS is based on TLV values, been extended quite a lot. It support for extensions like MPLS-TE and GMPLS. Continual Expansion As mentioned, OSPF and ISIS extended quite a lot extension drafts written regularly will continue to be. EIGRP doesn't have many of advanced options these two do. Scalability OSPF scales better than EIGRP with its use of areas however, don't think this really matters (like convergence time aregument, due to BFD). Not many people running 10k routes in one area in OSPF. Typically I would use IGP for fast routing within given part of network, but ultimately iBGP carries all internal routes. Every single router doesn't need every internal route in its RIB sourced via OSPF if you have hundreds or thousands or routers, some of far away (topologically speaking) it's worthless knowing about them. Interoperability Lastly reason EIGRP is/was a Cisco proprietary technology. this recently submitted into draft for other software vendors to start incorporating, it's too late (I believe).No currently running network to waste huge sums money switching from other IGP to EIGRP, I don't know why new network would consider it (if mixing Cisco equipment with non-Cisco). Simply because non-Cisco equipment supports OSPF has been doing so for years. code is tried and test, many bugs fixed, oodles of information on line etc. It will take years for EIGRP to catch up (if't too late already!).

Area 0 chosen to backbone, number 0 or 0. 0. 0. 0 is just a number. OSPF is link state LSDB must be identical within area. to ensure SPF calculation consistent and to prevent routing loops. If running single area OSPF any area can be used, no requirement to have area 0. running multi area OSPF, ABR must be used. ABR is router with adjacency in area 0 and at least one other area. ABRs take type 1 and 2 LSAs announce them as type 3 summary LSAs in other areas. not summarization of prefixes, it's summary of topological information. in distance vector behaviour. other areas don't have full information about each other all inter area traffic must pass through area 0. Otherwise could be routing loops because not having full topology. Due to design OSPF does not have to run full SPF when links go up/down in other areas. increases scalability.

One reason I've seen often is clarity: all routes carried within one routing protocol (BGP), IS-IS, OSPF or RIP only used for adjacency. no need to redistribute routes from one routing protocol to another.

suggest right answer is depends on topology of network. OSPF requires area boundaries to do summarization, if you doing green field network or topology condusive to drawing areas out use it. If network requires spokes to connect to multiple hubs, OSPF is harder to do, when I had this requirement on my frame relay network I migrated remote sites to BGP. wanted to use EIGRP and stub routers but cisco mentioned more resources spent on BGP-OSPF interoperability vs EIGRP-OSPF interoperability so I went BGP on basis. Another way to put it is EIGRP with stub routers and ability to summarize wherever you want will scale better in 'messy' topology.

When OSPF must carry non-backbone routes through backbone, uses distance-vector behavior (i. parts Bellman Ford algorithm) to propagate Type3 LSA metrics into non-backbone areas. example of OSPF's distance-vector behavior: <-- Area 5 --><- Area 0 --><- Area 4 --> R5-----------R1-----------R2------------R3---------------------R4 Cost 3 Cost 5 Cost 7 Cost 12 LSA--> LSA--> Type3 LSA Type3 LSA {From R1} {From R2} R5 cost is 3 R5 cost is 8 Consider what happens to /32 Loopback route for R5. R5 sends Type1 LSA containing /32 Loopback R1 (Area 5 ABR), connected to Area 0; it translates Type1 LSA into Type3 LSA with cost of 3.R2 (Area 4 ABR) receives R1's Type3 LSA (metric 3) changes metric to R5's Loopback, based on R2's cost to R1. Now R2's Type3 LSA for R5 has cost of 8. This is distance-vector behavior mentioned above. Requiring all non-backbone routes to go through backbone is a loop-prevention mechanism. Connecting non-backbone OSPF areas at ABR If 2 areas aren't connected through area 0 (discontiguous), OSPF as link state protocol increase possibility of routing loops?, OSPF uses distance-vector behavior to send routes through Area 0 backbone. Distance-vector protocols have limits, count-to-infinity problem. OSPF would be vulnerable to same issues, if didn't boundaries on behavior. 1RFC 3509 describes Cisco IOS's ABR behavior

You can read about finer workings of these protocols for yourself, they thoroughly documented on Internet it's a doddle to find information on them. From practicle perspective in case of EIGRP vs OSPF, OSPF always wins for following reasons: Convergence Speed: Everyone mentioned EIGRP faster than OSPF using default settings. If deploy either protocol without reading about them and use their default settings, you clearly don't know what you are doing in my opinion. Why deploy default settings without knowing what they are, when realise what they are realise OSPF supports BFD becomes lightening quick (as does ISIS). Traffic Engineering: OSPF like ISIS is based on TLV values, been extended quite a lot. It support for extensions like MPLS-TE and GMPLS. Continual Expansion As mentioned, OSPF and ISIS extended quite a lot extension drafts written regularly will continue to be. EIGRP doesn't have many of advanced options these two do. Scalability OSPF scales better than EIGRP with its use of areas however, don't think this really matters (like convergence time aregument, due to BFD). Not many people running 10k routes in one area in OSPF. Typically I would use IGP for fast routing within given part of network, but ultimately iBGP carries all internal routes. Every single router doesn't need every internal route in its RIB sourced via OSPF if you have hundreds or thousands or routers, some of far away (topologically speaking) it's worthless knowing about them. Interoperability Lastly reason EIGRP is/was a Cisco proprietary technology. this recently submitted into draft for other software vendors to start incorporating, it's too late (I believe).No currently running network to waste huge sums money switching from other IGP to EIGRP, I don't know why new network would consider it (if mixing Cisco equipment with non-Cisco). Simply because non-Cisco equipment supports OSPF has been doing so for years. code is tried and test, many bugs fixed, oodles of information on line etc. It will take years for EIGRP to catch up (if't too late already!).

Area 0 chosen to backbone, number 0 or 0. 0. 0. 0 is just a number. OSPF is link state LSDB must be identical within area. to ensure SPF calculation consistent and to prevent routing loops. If running single area OSPF any area can be used, no requirement to have area 0. running multi area OSPF, ABR must be used. ABR is router with adjacency in area 0 and at least one other area. ABRs take type 1 and 2 LSAs announce them as type 3 summary LSAs in other areas. not summarization of prefixes, it's summary of topological information. in distance vector behaviour. other areas don't have full information about each other all inter area traffic must pass through area 0. Otherwise could be routing loops because not having full topology. Due to design OSPF does not have to run full SPF when links go up/down in other areas. increases scalability.

According to my knowledge only possible to crack WPA/WPA2 PSK or Pre Shared Keys. During authentication handshake. possible to capture eapol handshakes. can be accomplished either actively or passively., just aircrack not sufficient. used in a last stage. not recommended to use PSK or similar lower level security for enterprise networks. not compatible with compliance requirements. Most these networks have main components as radius servers, PKIs with protocol support as EAP_TLS (Transport Layer Security). ensure authentication and trust among devices. With AES encryption standards, data communication is highly secure. not possible to crack if it up to its standards., may be vulnerable spots. Like mixed protocol usage, obsolete clients who allowed to use other mechanisms. Nothing is 100% secure.

Not alone like a WPA/2 PSK attack, where you can simply capture handshake and bruteforce. need to capture "Enterprise" authentication attempt. To do this, can perform "Evil Twin" attack captures authentication attempt, can then be subsequently cracked. excellent presentation by Matt Neely of SecureState details attack: http://www. slideshare. net/NEOISF/attacking-and-securing-wpa-enterpris Specific Steps of Attack: Attacker sets up a Fake AP Mirror target SSID, encryption type and band Configure AP to accept Enterprise authentication Enable AP, ensure it visible to target Connect AP to FreeRADIUS (with password Wireless Pwnage Edition patch) server captures auth Deauth any target within range of your fake AP Wait for targets to attach to fake AP, capture their authentication Crack challenge / response pair to recover password Hope this helps!

believe WPA was original WPA standard, WPA2 was improved version of it. Some network cards can’t connect to WPA2 networks. From Wikipedia page on WPA: later WPA2 certification mark indicates compliance with full IEEE 802. 11i standard. This advanced protocol not work with some older network cards. Wikipedia article cites white paper from Wi-Fi Alliance: WPA is both forward and backward-compatible designed to run on existing Wi-Fi devices as software download. In nutshell, WPA/WPA2 network will any network card that supports WPA or WPA2 to connect to it; WPA2 only network locks out network cards only support newer standard. don’t think meaningful difference in security., I’ve used WPA2 Personal on my Airport Extreme since bought it, no device ever had problems connecting. Confession: initially misread question as about difference between Personal and Enterprise, wrote this. not directly answering question, include it for interest. “Personal” and “Enterprise” refer to two flavours of WPA and WPA2. From Wi-fi Alliance’s page on WPA2: WPA2 can be enabled in two versions - WPA2 Personal and WPA2 Enterprise. WPA2 - Personal protects unauthorized network access by utilizing set-up password. WPA2 - Enterprise verifies network users through server. WPA2 is backward compatible with WPA. believe WPA and WPA2 both come in these two flavours, hence either/or. Personal is more suitable for home network, but less secure than enterprise. Enterprise connects to “RADIUS server” for authentication. don’t know what that is, but sounds clever and secure. guess device connecting to your Time Capsule sees request for WPA2 password, hence why it doesn’t ask you for WPA2 Personal password.
If I was you I'd visit this web page set up Mac for access to new WPA2 Enterprise Wi-Fi network at University of Alabama, but then would be cheating.

Both 'WPA' and 'WPA2' use AES to encrypt information transiting WiFi network, but WPA uses TKIP to manage keys to encrypt data. TKIP is vulnerable to attack (it not secure) and should not be used. WPA2 uses AES-CCMP for key management. "WPA/WPA2 Personal", also called mixed-mode, allows negotiation of key management modes and reduces security of network to lowest common denominator. BOTTOM LINE: If concerned about security/privacy of information on networks (wired and wireless), DON'T use WPA or WPA/WPA2. Use WPA2 only., if't, WEP is basically same as no security at all. poster points out 'Enterprise' modes send authentication requests to server before allowing client on network. two big advantages are: central management: I don't have to set keys on every access point, and can disable accounts of individual users. traceability: I know which WiFi device belongs to which user. longer keys (like 2048 bit, versus 128 for 'personal'). This decreases likelihood attacker can figure out key in time it's in use. 'personal' pre-shared key ("PSK") is derived from passphrase you type into client, even if PSK allowed long keys, you'd have to type passphrase most people would object to.

As you noticed, it doesn't have symbols, makes it weaker than a password of similar length does, but no other 'obvious' defect with this password. password does not have to use symbols to be strong, as long as it's long enough (obligatory XKCD link)., now this password appears in plain text on website (dedicated to passwords), likely some attackers will include it in dictionary., might be users less proficient in English, or audacious types, still use this password since it looks random and reasonably long., saying "Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ is a weak password" is self-fulfilling prophecy.

curious about same thing, put Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ into Google, lo! behold it found something wasn't just a paraphrase of "Don't use this password" advice — password itself was embedded in example source code that showed how you could send a password to a server! (link to page, and screenshot below) real goal of advice is not that Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ is a mysteriously weak password because of keyboard layout or low entropy or doesn't include symbols or Unicode or emoji: It's simply to remind you you should never use a password's been published somewhere, especially one published as "example" password! [Update: This is intentionally a screenshot and not simply a code snippet; content of code is less important than seeing how it appeared verbatim on's website!]

misleading statement. "Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ" is a strong password in practice. It won't be caught by anything but brute force attack on (no dictionary words) and it's sixteen characters, above common standards I see (8 or 6). This password might only be considered weak if attacker knew no symbols were used. If account this password attached to publicly says "only numbers and cap/lowercase letters" this password might seem weaker for sake of example, but it's actually still better than 8 digit password. So, for 16 character password using capital letters, lowercase letters, and 0-9 digits, entropy is 6216 = (48 × 1027) vs using 8 characters password with all symbols (we'll assume 96, not 72 characters) is 968 = (7 × 1015). massive difference. reason for confusion is example is oversimplifying basic advice to use capital, lowercase, digit, and symbol. In actuality, length of password is more critical and in practice attacker would not be able to know full character set wasn't used and would still have to brute force 9616.

While Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ is certainly a poor choice of password now, seeing your question has generated of activity on Stack Exchange and widely published the password, I don't any discernible reason we can pin down for why this website would say it's bad in first place, because, it is not a credible source. source you're drawing from appears to be a loosely organized list of security tips of low to middling quality. Some tips are good (e. g. use 2-step authentication whenever possible, lock your computer and mobile phone when you leave them), but some questioned by security experts (e. g. change your passwords every 10 weeks, use at least one uppercase/lowercase/number/symbol) and a few seem downright paranoid (e. g. tip 22, states if a WiFi router in home, nearby attackers can detect passwords you're typing in because of changes in WiFi signal from moving your hands, and using an on-screen keyboard with random layouts will mitigate this). it probably not an issue that most of tips are poorly proofread (with many spelling errors and punctuation inconsistencies), it an issue that absolutely none of tips are cited, whole website is anonymous. no quotes from security experts, no articles we can read up on for further information or discussion. website contains no author information - nowhere on website, or even in website's Whois registration, any way to contact the author or know who they are. This means we have little to no way of determining how good of a tip "Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ is a weak password" is, or what it means. no way to contact the author of this website and ask them ourselves, doubt it would be useful to do so.I think we best off ignoring this suggestion, taking way only fact that Gbt3fC79ZmMEFUFJ should not be used because we have talked about it at such length. TL;DR: Passwordsgenerator. net is just another anonymous stranger on Internet - ignore it. As addendum, you may be interested in some other things I found when inspecting website itself, to get better context on it perhaps find more information on it. found wasn't pleasant: website provides an option (default checked, but still) to not generate password on server. This is simply false. Entropy is function of number of possible symbols, AND length. If generated at random, entropy (in bits) can be calculated by log2(number-of-symbolslength). For alpha-numberic with variable case, this is simply log2(6216), or about 95. rub most passwords are NOT generated at random, this simple formula isn't often useful.

easiest way to do this is to make an album into you put all photos you want to keep, then drag and drop them from Photos into a folder on your hard drive. To strictly answer your question, not possible to delete something from your device have it remain accessible from iCloud Photo Library. more details: idea behind iCloud Photos Library is to have all your photos on all your devices. Picture a parent of a small family in California who takes, on average, several photos a week has a Mac, iPad, and iPhone. When they take a photo on their iPhone, it syncs to their other two devices automatically so when they arrive home, they can open computer and view photos or videos they took. cool? Yes, for some situations it's ideal. But problem, if you don't have enough storage on phone to hold all photos, iCloud Library stuck until you open settings and allow it to optimize your device storage. It then saves low resolution photos to device download high resolution version when you view photo. convenient in some situations. problem comes in when you want to control what photos go where. I've taken thousands of photos and videos on my iPhone don't want all of those on my phone. But with iCloud Library enabled, all of photos will be on your device no way to control what images are in cloud versus on your device., seems Apple's solution to problem of having too many photos and videos on phone would be to enable option to optimize device storage. However, by, biggest problem with iCloud Photo Library and "optimize device storage" option. If you enable that setting, and then to disable it at, it will attempt to download full resolution version of all your images (not just device-optimized high-resolution one). This, but causes problem as your device likely wouldn't have near enough storage by to handle that., probably not the approach you want to take. To summarize: use iCloud Photo Library if you don't take (or keep) a lot of photos and if have more than one Apple device. Otherwise, better to avoid it.

found methods on Ubuntu Forums in thread titled: Thread: How do I lock screen in XFCE?. excerpted from 2 of answers in thread Method #1 - Keyboard shortcut Open settings manager > keyboard > shortcuts default shortcut to lock screen is ctrl-alt-del. If want to change it, click add on left, type in name for your list of shortcuts, (widen window see whole thing) select xflock4 shortcut on right and enter new key combo. Method #2 - via command line $ xflock4 Method #3 - xscreenlock Most I use xscreenlock on multitude of Linux distros. It's fairly ubiquitous. excerpt from developers website XScreenSaver is standard screen saver collection shipped on most Linux and Unix systems running X11 Window System. released first version in 1992. ported it to MacOS X in 2006, and to iOS in 2012. On X11 systems, XScreenSaver is two things: it is large collection of screen savers; and also framework for blanking and locking screen. On MacOS systems, screen savers work with usual MacOS screen saving framework (X11 is not required). On iOS devices, it is application that lets you run each of demo modes manually. screenshot of main dialog. ton of screenshots of various screensavers and Xscreensaver also provides screen locking as well. http://www. jwz. org/xscreensaver/screenshots/

"Lock Screen" now available via Apple menu.

I set up my screen saver with "hot corner" in System Preferences (so screen saver starts when I move mouse into corner). This in combination with setting security for password to be "immediately" required, means you have simple way to lock screen.

two reasons in favor of using import module rather than from module import function. First is namespace. Importing function into global namespace risks name collisions. Second't relevant to standard modules, but significant for you own modules, especially during development. It's option to reload() a module. Consider: from module import func. reload(module) # func still points to old code On other hand import module. reload(module) # module. func points to new code for speed. importing only function needed rather than import whole module (which contains more useless functions python will waste time importing them) Whether import a module or import function from a module, Python will parse whole module. Either way module is imported. "Importing a function" is nothing more than binding function to a name. In import module less work for interpreter than from module import func.

Importing module doesn't waste anything; module is always fully imported (into sys. modules mapping), whether you use import sys or from sys import argv makes no odds. only difference between two statements is name is bound; import sys binds name sys to module (so sys -> sys. modules['sys']), from sys import argv binds different name, argv, pointing straight at attribute contained inside of module (so argv -> sys. modules['sys']. argv). rest of sys module is still there, whether you use anything else from module or not. no performance difference between two approaches., sys. argv has to look up two things; to look up sys in global namespace (finds module), then look up attribute argv., by using from sys import argv you can skip attribute lookup, since already have direct reference to attribute. But import statement still has to do that work, looks up same attribute when importing,'ll only need to use argv once. If had to use argv thousands of times in a loop, it could perhaps make a difference, but in this specific case does not., choice between one or the other should be based solely on coding style. In large module, I'd use import sys; code documentation matters, using sys. argv in large module makes it clearer what you referring to than just argv. If only place you use argv is in '__main__' block to call main() function, by use from sys import argv if feel happier about: if __name__ == '__main__': from sys import argv main(argv) I'd still use import sys there myself. All things being equal (and they are, exactly, in terms of performance and number of characters used to write it), that just easier on the eye for me.If importing something else altogether, perhaps performance comes into play. But only if use specific name in a module many times over, in a critical loop for example. creating local name (within function) to faster still: import somemodule def somefunction(): localname = somemodule. somefunctionorother while test: # huge, critical loop foo = localname(bar)

If it's bunch of pure functions, e. g. re, I put them in module. use a class when I know there's state want to keep with that code (e. g. a file gets read in once, whose data used by several functions).

difference between class variables and instance variables, is a question of who knows what?. An instance variable is only known (= bound) to concrete instance - hence the name. public class Person { private String firstName; private String lastName; [. ] } definition of a class is like a blueprint for building concrete objects. Perhaps point confuses you. But writing it this way, every variable bound to its concrete object:. Every person has its own firstName A class variable is - as name says - known to each and every member of a class; or known/ bound at class level. typical example is a counter of how many objects, you created - problematic example; but doesn't matter at this early stage. public class Person { private String firstName; private String lastName; [. ] static int numberOfPersons = 0 } numberOfPersons is declared static is keyword to distingush between class variables and instance variabes. variable is declared like others within class definition. But static keyword signals, it is different. firstName, lastName are instance variables and bound to concrete instance numberOfPersons is bound to class, so every instance could access this variable. tl;dr place where variables are defined is the class definition. Class variables are known at/bound to class level,. each concrete instance has access to it. To define a class variable, use keyword static. Instance variables only known at instance level. define them without static keyword. Further documentation for Java is here

Instance Variable: Instance variables declared in class, outside method, constructor or block. Instance variable belongs to instance class or belongs object. Instance variable separate value of each instance of class. Class InstanceDemo { // instance variable visible for any child class. public String name = "Testing"; count variable visible in Demo class only. private int count = 2; } Method to access instance variable: InstanceDemo demo = new InstanceDemo (); System. out. println("Access Instance variable: " + demo. count + ", "+demo. name ); Output: 2, Testing Class Variable: Class variable belongs to class. class variable created by adding “static” keyword before variable. Also called static variable. important class variable maintain single shared value for all instance of class, even if no instance object class exists. Class ClassDemo { // count variable is Same for all instance of class public static int count = 2; } Method to access class variable: System. out. println("Access Class variable: " + ClassDemo. count ); //class variable directly refer with class name Output: 2 Brief Difference Between Class Variable and Instance Variable: Instance variables have separate values for each instance of class. Class variables maintain single shared value for all instances class, even if no instance object class exists. use static keyword to change instance variable into class variable. Both instance and class variables declared at class level, not within methods.

Mail talks to mail server to show you messages. Only IMAP accounts can be synchronized as formal way for server and mail client on your mac to double check all messages to make sure everything in sync between two. Get mail focuses on Inbox relies on Mail app having "correct" view matching data on mail server. Synchronize allows for noise/errors/lost messages, incorrect statuses other real life bumps and errors. It double counts and double checks each every message to make sure things 100% correct. Synchronize also checks all folders recursively to get everything accounted for - not just subset of folders marked as having new mail. more "deep cleaning" be if you told mail to rebuild account or mailbox. means local storage mail uses on your mac has problems getting mail or synchronizing. It's last step before deleting account and starting over to download things cleanly from server. In - synchronize should normally do nothing - but it will fill in gaps as needed. (of course it will get new mail as part of total synchronization - but it's to be slower and use more resources on mac than just asking for new mail)

iCloud Mail service. Turning it on provides iCloud mail account for Mail. app to use, nothing more. basically automated method of entering iCloud mail server information into Mail. app to configure your @icloud. com email account, per Apple KB article: iCloud: Mail server information not sync other accounts - settings or emails of other accounts not affected by this setting, just your @icloud. com or @me. com account. read more about iCloud Mail at Apple KB article: iCloud: Mail overview

possible to synchronize email accounts between Macs. This iCloud Keychain is for. Activating it will sync over all your accounts (those listed in Mac Accounts settings). One problem is it is all or none setting. this doesn't help synchronize email accounts between Mac and iOS.

Get Mail only fetch for new mail in Inbox. Synchronize look for changes in IMAP configuration, look for changes in folder structure of your account, probably lot more. Edit: Synchronize should not be something you do every time you Mail. It's to force Mail to update conf/folders of IMAP account. Like if network and not syncing anymore. usually, when moving, deleting, etc. Mail is already care of updating where it needs to be updated.

You didn't do wrong, but point with rsync is after initial backup/copy, subsequent rsync runs clever to only copy/backup stuff's changed. say you do your 300GB backup, then a week later want to backup again, if you've only made 5GB of changes on your disk, rsync will only try to edit/backup this 5GB, rather than to copy over full 300GB again. This is time saving you benefit from when using rsync, only get it when running regular backups of same disk. answer to your question is no, for one off copy operation, rsync and finder likely to be exactly the same -, may be finder is slightly faster. Rsync is for keeping/maintaining up-to-date backup of working disk, time savings are in long-run, not taking initial backup. To get benefits from rsync, you should take a copy of your rsync command, store it in way you can run it again in future (for example, might embed it in a batch/script file can run periodically in future). next time you run same backup, it might take 5 minutes, since's unlikely you have changed that much on your disk. for example, here's content of script file I use to keep up-to-date backup of my music folder on my mac - set to run every 24 hours: #!/bin/bash rsync -ariv /Users/myuser/Music /Volumes/data/media/myuser first time I ran this it took ages, but now, when I run it again, it just backs up what's changed in my Music folder, might take a minute or two. Meanwhile, I know I've got a 100% up-to-date copy of my music folder in my backup drive I can go to should my primary drive fail.

not as ubiquitous as rsync, in past used a tool call "mpscp" - http://www. sandia. gov/MPSCP/mpscp_design. htm From Sandia National Labs, it's a file copy tool runs over SSH optimized to saturate high-speed networks between close systems (such copying terabytes of data between two supercomputers at same site, connected via 10Gb+ or Infiniband). Rsync widely used for backups mirroring as improved copy command for everyday use. In short: Yes, it can indeed be malicious! Accessing a site via HTTPS means connection between your computer and website's server is encrypted and secure. HTTPS does Encrypt data transmitted over network between your computer and website's server to prevent third parties from intercepting it. Prevent man in the middle attacks. HTTPS does not do HTTPS Does not scan content served by website for viruses or malicious elements its still possible for website's authors (or someone gained unauthorized access to website) to have website serve malicious content to your browser.

secure from https isn't related to content on a website/service. In, https helps us by making difficult for third party to know what information we exchanged with a website (and's why most banks utilize at least https on services), but that doesn't stop a website or service to be infected with malicious software or attacker to indirectly reach you by infecting server., I inferred from your question that when you used term 'secure' you meant it in different way (in sense of safety against malicious content), in, https does not protect you at because it doesn't pay attention to content (what transmitted through connection) itself.

Don't click through warnings. Don't accept invalid certificates. Use HTTPS Everywhere or Force-TLS to ensure using a HTTPS (i. e., SSL-encrypted) connection for everything related to site.

A session entirely over HTTPS is fairly safe, as all requests from browser, and pages transmitted by server are encrypted. However, when accessed via HTTPS, many sites only carry out authentication step over HTTPS, then drop back to HTTP for rest of session. So, your password itself is safe, but session ID used by server to identify you for session is transmitted in clear by your browser. This reduces load on webserver (because encryption/decryption is CPU-intensive) but makes site less secure. Gmail is safe uses HTTPS for whole session, but Facebook and many other sites do not. This tools as Firesheep able to hijack users' accounts when attacker sharing unencrypted wireless network. You can protect yourself from this attack by using a VPN to encrypt all session data, or by only using networks strong, per-user encryption such as WPA-PSK (WEP uses same key for every user, does not offer protection from this attack).

Not a guarantee. HTTPS means web page has SSL, simply means your connection to page is encrypted. content on page could be anything be posted on any web site whether encrypted by SSL or not. Additionally, as listed in answers in comments below, you can be fooled into false sense of security when (in different examples) target server is compromised, or a hacker redirects your https site data to different https encrypted location. You can still be encrypted to a site, but possibly even a fake site that looks like real one instead.
No, very nature of HTTPS is certificate required to decrypt it. You could sniff traffic, but it would be encrypted and useless to you.

In addition to other points raised, worth mentioning even a trusted site (for example, your bank), could still be infected by a virus makes it behave maliciously. even if you trust organization, https does not guarantee website doesn't do malicious things.

secure from https isn't related to content on a website/service. It called 'secure' because theoretically security protocols (ssl/tsl and others) do not allow information exchanged to be easily understood (it encrypts data flow), even if someone catch your packets, they would have to decrypt it to understand message. this useful because some information such as passwords, social security number, credit card number. can cause problems if discovered by someone intent on causing damage. In, https helps us by making difficult for third party to know what information we exchanged with a website (and's why most banks utilize at least https on services), but that doesn't stop a website or service to be infected with malicious software or attacker to indirectly reach you by infecting server., I inferred from your question that when you used term 'secure' you meant it in different way (in sense of safety against malicious content), in, https does not protect you at because it doesn't pay attention to content (what transmitted through connection) itself.

If're concerned about safely browsing to some site over insecure network, best steps take to ensure security are: Make sure site uses HTTPS, not HTTP. Make sure site has valid certificate. Don't click through warnings. Don't accept invalid certificates. Use HTTPS Everywhere or Force-TLS to ensure using a HTTPS (i. e., SSL-encrypted) connection for everything related to site.

This shows the power of math. It depends. need to understand this not security-by-obscurity: entropy values used in comic assume attacker knows you're using this method. If attacker doesn't know how you're generating passphrase, entropy goes up massively. trick to XKCD method is need to use a random number generator and a good word list: never pick words yourself, not even "randomly" (in quotes because humans are bad at picking things randomly, why you shouldn't do it). Diceware has tools to help you do this, takes random element out of computer's reach by using ordinary dice. Against broad-based attack -the of where attacker got a list of passwords from Website and doesn't know anything about whose passwords in list- this is as strong as it ever was., its strength comes from power of exponents (and a good word list). Schneier's attack can work, but only in entirely different context. His attack assumes you are being specifically targeted, by an attacker who already knows a great deal about you. This might not seem worrisome at first, because stereotypical determined attacker is an intelligence agent behind a screen, most of us don't have to worry so much about those: there are only so many of them, each one can only afford to care about so many people. But it's actually more of a problem than might first seem, thanks to advent of sophisticated malware. malware installation can afford to care about you even though attacker does not, you still wind up facing extremely determined attacker. Even more determined than human could be, in, though less creative. Malware that compiles information on you will give words that seem important to you high priority in word list. It does this because most people pick "random" words themselves, but in doing, they bias strongly toward words most important to them: may still "feel random, but some words are more likely to come up than others.For reason, giving these words high priority often results in quick hits, this is "trick" Schneier is talking about. However, you can thwart Schneier's attack by using real randomness. catch this requires discipline: all decisions about what words to use in your passphrase (aside from choosing good word list) must be taken out of your hands. This things like Diceware can help you.

Ole' Bruce wants to assert his scheme is the One and Only, best, winner, ultimate scheme., he needs to say disparaging things about "competitors", regardless of whether assertions scientifically sound or not. In this case, always assumed password generation method is known to attacker. That's whole point of entropy computations; see analysis. attackers are "on to this trick" changes nothing (when attacker knows password generation method, entropy computation describes exactly password strength; when attacker is incompetent and does not know password generation method, password strength is only higher, by amount nigh impossible to quantify). quip about "passwords in memory" is more incoherent ramblings. Passwords necessarily go to RAM at point, whether you type them or copy-paste from password safe, or similar. guess is Bruce was drunk. Update Schneier was asked to comment about his passphrase condemnation in a Reddit AMA (via archive. org, original link) August 2, 2016. He continued to advocate for his password creation system as superior alternative to random word passphrases. Schneier his scheme "gives more entropy per memorizable character than other methods" true when compared to characters making up words. But also irrelevant when system relies on memorizing words rather than characters, and you're allowed to combine enough words to generate adequate 'entropy' for your passphrase as a whole.

If want to achieve 90 bits of "effective strength" then 77 bits of password strength should do it. achieved with a six word Diceware password (77. 5-bits) from original list and 84. 6 bits with six words drawn from list of 17679 words. don't expect most people to use passwords that long. expect people will use things 4 or 5 words long. but if genuinely worried about NSA going after passwords, six words should be sufficient assuming use decent password hashing scheme. rough estimates only didn't spend time researching costs and benchmarks. lots things in my estimates to quibble with. attempted to be conservative (pessimistic about scheme I'm advocating). been vague about "well-hashed passwords"., I'm very conservative with respect to password hashing in 1Password. Back in 2008, I described "Schneier scheme"'s it. Ole' Bruce wants to assert his scheme is the One and Only, best, winner, ultimate scheme., he needs to say disparaging things about "competitors", regardless of whether assertions scientifically sound or not. In this case, always assumed password generation method is known to attacker. That's whole point of entropy computations; see analysis. attackers are "on to this trick" changes nothing (when attacker knows password generation method, entropy computation describes exactly password strength; when attacker is incompetent and does not know password generation method, password strength is only higher, by amount nigh impossible to quantify). quip about "passwords in memory" is more incoherent ramblings. It depends. need to understand this not security-by-obscurity: entropy values used in comic assume attacker knows you're using this method. If attacker doesn't know how you're generating passphrase, entropy goes up massively. trick to XKCD method is need to use a random number generator and a good word list: never pick words yourself, not even "randomly" (in quotes because humans are bad at picking things randomly, why you shouldn't do it). Diceware has tools to help you do this, takes random element out of computer's reach by using ordinary dice. Against broad-based attack -the of where attacker got a list of passwords from Website and doesn't know anything about whose passwords in list- this is as strong as it ever was., its strength comes from power of exponents (and a good word list). Schneier's attack can work, but only in entirely different context. His attack assumes you are being specifically targeted, by an attacker who already knows a great deal about you. This might not seem worrisome at first, because stereotypical determined attacker is an intelligence agent behind a screen, most of us don't have to worry so much about those: there are only so many of them, each one can only afford to care about so many people. But it's actually more of a problem than might first seem, thanks to advent of sophisticated malware. malware installation can afford to care about you even though attacker does not, you still wind up facing extremely determined attacker. Even more determined than human could be, in, though less creative. Malware that compiles information on you will give words that seem important to you high priority in word list. It does this because most people pick "random" words themselves, but in doing, they bias strongly toward words most important to them: may still "feel random, but some words are more likely to come up than others.For reason, giving these words high priority often results in quick hits, this is "trick" Schneier is talking about. However, you can thwart Schneier's attack by using real randomness. catch this requires discipline: all decisions about what words to use in your passphrase (aside from choosing good word list) must be taken out of your hands. This things like Diceware can help you.

only weak argument I can of to reject such a CVV would be if someone trying to brute-force your 3-digit code, they might start with 000 first (but would also reject 001?). From practical point of view, how reasonable it to decline "000" as insecure? It's not really reasonable. Either you can charge card with provided CVC/CVV code or you can't. no good reason to reject this code, since it is valid, and can't be sure if credit card's codes are valid until you try to charge it., poorly-designed input validation is too common. Some developers tendency to assume certain values are invalid without checking spec, or not properly unit test input validations. examples include: IP address 1. 1. 1. 1 Version checking bugs like "10" < "9" if only first character in string is checking Names with non-alpha character (like apostrophe in my name) not uncommon people in customer service will respond to bug reports with "that's not a bug, it's a feature" without consulting developers.

I currently have a credit card that arguably has a worse CVV number: 123 it never been denied, but from a security point of view I don't like it as feel like it could be the first thing a thief would type in if they had my numbers but not my card. From website's point of view, IMHO it's asinine to purposely treat a valid number as invalid. (Even more if the chances of it occurring are merely 1 in 1000. ) be easy for site to attempt a small authorization to confirm credit card, or let hotel decide for themselves, I don't agree with "preventing fake numbers" argument., quick search yields few people with the same issue on various websites over years., you're not alone. :)

They can't admit it. one example: say, somewhere in stack, they use language with untyped variables (i. e. Where same variable can hold 123. 45, "late for dinner", 0-character string, "undefined" token, etc).'s commonplace to write this: if ($CVC) # is CVC field present? In untyped language, blank string evaluates to 0 (false) as programmer intended, but so does 000! better ways to do that. In this case, problem is not in public-facing web UI use, but in back-end platform both of you share. agent should open bug on it in ticketing system. why did they claim what they said? Because normal businesses reluctant to admit this structural error that makes them look incompetent. Obviously it is wrong; proven by all other people you do business with who have no problem with it. But try it yourself; try competing booking platform and see how it goes.

Alexander O'Mara provided correct answer, but having worked in a hotel using booking. com I believe I can provide additional information about reason CVV denied. Every day hotel I worked in receive around 50 bookings, a quarter of these bookings using fake credit card details, about 90% of people using fake credit card details not show up. This resulted in guesswork when assigning rooms, we often try to guess if person will show up based on credit card details, also sometimes take into consideration name, location, how many days they staying, etc. We also try to call the day before to confirm bookings, so fake bookings result in minimal interruption to business. Blocking CVV 000 is just booking. com's lazy attempt to reduce amount fake bookings. Some other CVVs are blocked as well. reason why booking. com blocks CVV and other websites do not is because other websites generally attempt to charge credit card immediately, while booking. com only forwards information to hotels which charge credit card on day of arrival.

Consumer grade routers have this distinction, some enterprise SOHO routers also have this distinction. WAN stands for Wide Area Network network connects your router to your service provider. WAN port usually connects to a DSL modem, cable modem or fibre media converter. LAN stands for Local Area Network network connects devices within your home/business to the router. LAN port or ports usually connect to PCs, printers etc. LAN ports can also connect to wireless APs to allow laptops, smartphones, tablets etc to connect to LAN. router routes between LAN and WAN network, applying NAT and firewall policy in.

A LAN is typically within your own premises (your organization's campus, building, office suite, home), it's something you build and own yourself, down to the physical cabling. In contrast, a WAN is connects between geographically separated locations, you generally to lease access to lines or data transmission services from telecommunications carriers to create your WAN. shorter distances needed for on-premises networks, focus on connecting PCs and servers, LANs to be built on Ethernet and other 802. 3-family (and 802. 11-family) physical layers and data links. 1000BASE-T, 1000BASE-SX, 1000BASE-LX, etc. off-premises network links need to go longer distances and work over telecommunication carriers' existing infrastructure, they tend to use physical and data-link standards more common in telecom industry., for your convenience, telecom carriers usually hand off to you using an 802. 3-family link, even if they using behind scenes is, OC-3 and SONET/SDH. of technical hurdles associated with moving lots of data long distances reliably, WAN links tend to be lower bandwidth and higher latency than LAN links., you usually paying a separate telecom carrier for service, to keep costs down, most organizations try to limit (or not go crazy with) how much data they move over WAN links. differences between LANs and WANs at physical and data-link layers. At the network layer (Layer 3 in old OSI layering model), most people use IP (Internet Protocol) nowadays.it all uses IP, applications use IP don't have to know physical and data-link layers in use, anything you can do on a LAN you can potentially do on a WAN as well, if you have high enough bandwidth low enough latency for trying to do, as long as you haven't blocked it at your firewall (or via accidentally firewall-like properties of NAT).
allows use of AirPlay from outside private network. WAN= Wide Area Network.

Nothing much will change in to WAN exposure, as long as you're not configuring server to proxy or route traffic. Services intended for LAN only should be configured to only run on appropriate interface, regardless of firewall in place. increased risk if one of externally facing services is compromised, potentially allowing access to resources on LAN. If want to be careful you can set up firewall on the Mac to not allow traffic out LAN interface unless it originated on the Mac.

router is layer 3 device i. e It cannot modify IP address of packet, can only change MAC Address can route packet, gateway could be NAT capable, or can act as a firewall in case of NAT-capable gateway can change packet's IP address more capable gateways can block traffic Layer2 Devices - Switches Layer3 Devices - Routers Layer2- Layer7 Devices - Gateways/Firewalls/IDC (usually implement DPI -deep packet inspection) Gateways distinct from routers or switches communicate using more than one protocol can operate at any layer of 7 layer OSI model of networking. - Wikipedia

Apple Support Airport Express FAQ: Question: AirPort Express only has one Ethernet port, does it act as a LAN port, WAN port, or both? English words have overlapping meanings but slightly different implications. Property implies something possessed by something else. Attribute suggests inherent characteristic. However, because their meanings almost completely overlap, you can substitute one for other. exception where terms are jargon, for example in C# where property and attribute have different, more specific, meanings. both are member variables, both associated with a class., differences between two: Instance variables: belong to instance of a class, object. every instance of class has's own copy of variable. Changes to variable don't reflect in other instances of class. public class Product { public int Barcode; } Class variables: also known as static member variables only one copy of variable shared with all instances of class. If changes made to variable, all other instances see effect of changes. public class Product { public static int Barcode; } Full example: // INSTANCE VARIABLE public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Product prod1 = new Product(); prod1. Barcode = 123456; Product prod2 = new Product(); prod2. Barcode = 987654; System. out. println(prod1. Barcode); System. out. println(prod2. Barcode); } } public class Product { public int Barcode; } output: 123456 987654, change instance variable to a class variable by making it static: //CLASS VARIABLE public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Product prod1 = new Product(); prod1. setBarcode(123456); Product prod2 = new Product(); prod2. setBarcode(987654); System. out. println(prod1. getBarcode()); System. out. println(prod2. getBarcode()); } } public class Product { public static int Barcode; public int getBarcode() { return Barcode; } public void setBarcode(int value){ Barcode = value; } } used non-static methods to get and set value of Barcode to call it from object not from class. output following: 987654 987654

difference between class variables and instance variables, is a question of who knows what?. An instance variable is only known (= bound) to concrete instance - hence the name. public class Person { private String firstName; private String lastName; [. ] } definition of a class is like a blueprint for building concrete objects. Perhaps point confuses you. But writing it this way, every variable bound to its concrete object:. Every person has its own firstName A class variable is - as name says - known to each and every member of a class; or known/ bound at class level. typical example is a counter of how many objects, you created - problematic example; but doesn't matter at this early stage. public class Person { private String firstName; private String lastName; [. ] static int numberOfPersons = 0 } numberOfPersons is declared static is keyword to distingush between class variables and instance variabes. variable is declared like others within class definition. But static keyword signals, it is different. firstName, lastName are instance variables and bound to concrete instance numberOfPersons is bound to class, so every instance could access this variable. tl;dr place where variables are defined is the class definition. Class variables are known at/bound to class level,. each concrete instance has access to it. To define a class variable, use keyword static. Instance variables only known at instance level. define them without static keyword. Further documentation for Java is here

explained here (with example Bicycle class with class variable numberOfBicycles and instance variables cadence, speed, gear & id): Sometimes, want to have variables common to all objects. This accomplished with static modifier. Fields have static modifier in declaration are called static fields or class variables. associated with class, rather than with any object. Every instance of class shares class variable, in one fixed location in memory. Any object can change value of class variable, but class variables can be manipulated without creating instance of class. class variable (declared static) is a location common to all instances. In example, numberOfBicycles is a class variable (since declared static). only one such variable (i. location) common to all instances and to class. if modify numberOfBicycles in one method, other methods see new value (even for different Bicycle objects) In contrast gear & id are instance variables (because declaration has no static modifier). Every Bicycle object has its own one. If modify gear for some Bicycle a, if b is another instance, modifying a. gear has no effect on b. gear Each Java object is distinct memory zone with meta data (e. reference to its class) and its own instance variables (perhaps inherited from superclass). But class variables are common to class shared by all instances. See also Object (computer science) & Instance variable wikipages.

Abstract Data Type: ADT may be defined as a set of data values and associated operations precisely specified independent of implementation. an Abstract Data Type is an organized collection of information and a set of operations to manage information. The set of operations defines interface of ADT. as ADT fulfills conditions of interface, it doesn’t matter how ADT is implemented., in ADT, data values and operations are defined with mathematical precision, rather than as implementation in computer language, we may reason about effects of operations, relations to other abstract data types whether program implements data type etc. simplest abstract data type is the stack data type for functions might be provided to create empty stack, to push values onto a stack and pop values from a stack. basic difference between abstract data type (ADT) and concrete data type is latter allow us to look at concrete representation, former hide representation from us. An ADT may be pure ADT or Updatable ADT. A pure ADT is one where all operations are pure functions. means operations have no side effects. In, they do not modify or update input arguments. They just use these arguments to generate output, are fresh values of ADT (or of other types). Most concrete types are pure. For example, no operation on integers modifies an integer. Instead, all operations like ‘+’ produce fresh outputs. An updatable ADT is one where some operations change values of ADT. For example, suppose operation called ‘pop’ that took a stack as argument modified it., “destructively”) by removing highest priority item. This operation would be considered impure and whole ADT would be impure also. An ADT may be user defined ADT. an Abstract Data Type is a data type that satisfies following two conditions: representation, or definition, of type and operations are contained in a single syntactic unit.representation of objects of type is hidden from program units use type, only direct operations possible on objects are provided in type’s definition. user defined Abstract Data Type should provide: type definition that allows program units to declare variables of type, but hides representation of these variables. set of operations for manipulating objects of type. example of user defined abstract data type is structure. ’C’ provides four basic types: int, char, float and double., ‘C’ also provides programmer ability to define his/her own types. Structure is one such example. structure is an aggregate of different parts, each part is of some existing type. struct abc {int x; float y; }; above structure definition does not create variables, rather creates new type. Variables of this type may be created in similar way to variables of built in type. struct abc a; typedef keyword allows to create new type names for new types. For example: typedef struct abc AB; where AB is new type name can now be used to create new types. AB b; Data Structures: characteristic features of data structures: contains component data items, may be atomic or another data structure (still domain). set of operations on one or more of component items. Defines rules as to how components relates to each other and to structure as a whole (assertions). Data Structures: data structure may be static or dynamic. static data structure has fixed size. meaning different from meaning of static modifier. Arrays are static; once define number of elements can hold, number doesn’t change. dynamic data structure grows and shrinks at execution time as required by contents. dynamic data structure implemented using links. Data structures may be categorized into linear data structures and non-linear data structures.In linear data structures every component has unique predecessor successor, except first and last elements, in non-linear data structures, no such restriction as elements may be arranged in any desired fashion restricted by way we use to represent such types.

English words have overlapping meanings but slightly different implications. Property implies something possessed by something else. Attribute suggests inherent characteristic. However, because their meanings almost completely overlap, you can substitute one for other. exception where terms are jargon, for example in C# where property and attribute have different, more specific, meanings. In HTML, something specifically called a tag attribute calling it a property confusing. If inventing new jargon for specific context, I to prefer whichever sounds more natural. If it's something discrete something else contains, I'd generally prefer property. If it's something inseparable inherent characteristic of something else (and especially if something other things can have as well), I'd generally prefer attribute.
